headline: NY mayor proposes closure of Rikers Island by 2032
summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a plan to shut the Rikers Island jail complex by 2032, relocating inmates to smaller facilities across four boroughs as part of a broader reform of New York’s correctional system.

headline: Car crashes into pedestrians on Brisbane’s Elizabeth Street
summary: A vehicle veered onto the footpath of Elizabeth Street in Brisbane’s CBD shortly before 7 pm, striking a group of pedestrians. Police are investigating the incident.

headline: Kushner says Russia open to NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine
summary: Jared Kushner stated that Russia appears “comfortable” with the idea of a NATO-like security guarantee for Ukraine, noting that former President Donald Trump is open to the concept, though details remain unclear.

headline: Tinned food and long-life milk boost Australian retail sales
summary: Official data shows that sales of long-life milk and tinned food rose in October after the “Be Ready” campaign, indicating a consumer shift toward stocked, shelf-stable items.

headline: New pill hailed as breakthrough for pancreatic cancer
summary: A drug called daraxonrasib showed promising results in a trial, making cancer undetectable in one-in-12 patients and halting tumour growth in almost all participants, marking a major advance in pancreatic cancer treatment.

headline: AFL draft night sees surprise pick of Brisbane academy prospect
summary: The AFL draft opened with a shock selection as Sydney chose Brisbane academy prospect Caylen Murray, sparking excitement among fans. The event continued with live interviews from school graduations as the second round got underway, highlighting the league’s emerging talent pool.

headline: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over possible chip exports to China
summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued a subpoena to Nvidia as part of an investigation into whether the company’s advanced semiconductor chips were exported to China, potentially breaching U.S. export restrictions. The probe follows internal turmoil after the departure of co-founder Jensen Huang.

headline: Former RAAF pilot accused of wife murder led police on wild goose chase
summary: In court, a former Royal Australian Air Force pilot charged with murdering his wife was described as a liar who deliberately misled police, sending investigators on a wild goose chase in an attempt to conceal his actions.

headline: Five teenagers charged with murder of 19-year-old woman
summary: A court heard the case of five teenagers accused of killing a 19-year-old woman. The youths face serious charges as the legal process unfolds, drawing attention to youth-related violent crime.

summary: Coastal communities in California issued hazard warnings after a series of low-pressure systems generated swells exceeding nine metres. Beaches and piers were closed as wave heights topped 30 ft, prompting safety alerts for residents and visitors.

headline: British Library to outsource security and convert reading rooms to business space
summary: The British Library announced plans to transfer its security staff to a private contractor and repurpose three public reading rooms as hireable business spaces, despite recent public funding for the facilities. The move has sparked union opposition.

headline: Netflix hires Australian to produce American football series, citing tax offset
summary: Netflix paid Australian Tom Farrah to develop an American-football project, leveraging a location tax offset that encourages high-budget productions to film in Australia. The deal highlights the country’s growing appeal to international media firms.

headline: Restrictions on reporting family law cases highlighted by journalists
summary: Reporters note that coverage of Federal Circuit and Family Court matters is heavily restricted, making it difficult to shed light on complex family-law issues. The piece calls for greater transparency in the judicial system.

headline: Heavy rain and storms batter Melbourne and wider Victoria
summary: Melbourne and surrounding parts of Victoria experienced intense rainfall and storm activity, prompting weather warnings across the state. The downpours caused disruptions and heightened concerns about flooding in affected areas.

headline: Teen accused in Logan shooting appears in court, others absent
summary: One of five 16-year-old boys charged with a Logan shooting appeared in court, while the remaining defendants did not apply for bail, leaving the case pending further legal proceedings.

summary: Prime listings in Sydney’s eastern suburbs highlight coastal walks, beach proximity, easy CBD access, vibrant food scenes and strong community appeal, offering buyers a blend of lifestyle and convenience.

summary: British retail sales rose 0.7% in October, driven by a surge in purchases of tinned food and long-life milk after the government’s ‘Be Ready’ campaign urged households to keep three days of supplies.

summary: British chef Rick Stein reflects on why his restaurants have thrived in Australia for nearly 60 years, citing personal ties and market appeal that have eluded other famous chefs.

summary: A secret lunch hosted by Eddie McGuire sparked a high-stakes battle over Michelin stars, ultimately revealing that Victoria could not afford the costly guide and the push failed.

headline: Thomas Markle's prison conditions compared to Sandringham House

summary: A rare supercell storm on the Eyre Peninsula ripped shed doors off, destroyed crops and knocked down major electricity transmission towers. Farmers describe their properties as “completely flattened” and are tallying losses as recovery efforts begin.

summary: Apple announced plans for an AI-driven assistant that can handle flight bookings and online shopping, following the success of Meta’s Muse and a surge in tools that let AI control Mac computers and write software.

summary: Economists question the relevance of a World War Two-era recession definition as Australia shows rising GDP alongside falling employment. The discussion highlights the lack of a formal recession metric and its implications for policy.

summary: The historic link between crude prices and borrowing costs has weakened, with oil losing influence over bond yields amid a widening “inflation virus” that is affecting markets globally.

summary: The upcoming vote on the UN secretary-general candidate could see the permanent five members block the Costa Rican frontrunner, reigniting debate over the P5’s dominance in the organisation.

summary: Guidance on household hygiene explains the factors that determine how frequently bedding and mattresses need washing, helping readers maintain a fresh sleeping environment.

summary: Analysts warn that Nvidia’s pivotal role in AI infrastructure mirrors the pre-crisis influence of AIG, raising concerns about systemic risk as the chip maker’s services become integral to the emerging AI economy.

summary: The Senate approved the BAAJA permitting reform legislation, a key step before it moves to the House and the President, with strong support from the artificial-intelligence and energy sectors.

summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has asked Google to take down a video featuring convicted rapist Russell Brand after victims complained about the content. Google has so far refused to comply with the request.

summary: The Crown’s closing address was presented to the jury in the trial of former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, accused of a cold-blooded double murder, as the case moves into its final phase.

headline: Denmark approves Greenland-US security pact
summary: The Danish parliament unanimously ratified a new Arctic security agreement linking Greenland, Denmark and the United States, aiming to modernise defence cooperation and reduce uncertainty over the strategically important territory.

headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic trilateral meeting in China
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen for a trilateral summit, discussing international peace and nuclear weapons, with Trump describing Putin as a friend.

headline: Hedge fund links AI model release to cyber-attack surge
summary: A leading hedge fund attributes the recent exponential rise in cyber-attacks to the release of a large-language AI model, suggesting the technology is being weaponised by threat actors.

headline: SanDisk to split shares after market close
summary: Memory-chip maker SanDisk will implement a stock split following Thursday’s market close, a move that will not change the company’s underlying fundamentals for shareholders.

headline: UK inquiry says lack of early border controls left nation vulnerable
summary: A Covid-19 inquiry concluded that the United Kingdom’s failure to impose early international border controls and delayed test-and-trace measures left the country “extremely vulnerable” and allowed rapid virus spread.

headline: McKenzie wins second Gold Walkley as The Age sweeps awards
summary: The Age’s McKenzie was awarded a second Gold Walkley after the publication secured two of the nine awards at the ceremony, with editor Patrick Elligett praising him as the best journalist of his generation.

headline: Deutsche Bank admits 2026 dollar forecast error, sees strength to 2027
summary: Deutsche Bank acknowledged its 2026 prediction of a weaker US dollar was wrong and now expects the dollar-strengthening forces that began in February to continue into early 2027, though a slowdown in AI growth could later undermine it.

headline: Badenoch defends comment linking amputee athletes to disability-benefit cuts
summary: UK minister Grant Badenoch said using double-amputee marathon runners to justify cuts to disability benefits was a “message of hope”, sparking criticism and a request for him to withdraw the remark.

headline: UK watchdog finds Viagogo may have used hidden fees
summary: Britain’s competition regulator provisionally concluded that ticket-reseller Viagogo employed drip-pricing, a practice that could constitute a breach of consumer-protection law.

headline: Meta removes posts after Guardian report on anti-vaccine group
summary: Meta has taken down posts from Children’s Health Defense, an anti-vaccine group led by Robert F Kennedy Jr., following a Guardian investigation that highlighted the group’s spread of false vaccine information.

headline: AFR wins Walkley for reporting KPMG scandal
summary: The Australian Financial Review earned a Walkley award for its investigative coverage of a scandal involving accounting firm KPMG, marking the publication’s second consecutive win for business reporting.

headline: Alibaba’s cloud profits eclipsed by AI lab losses
summary: Alibaba’s cloud services are delivering strong earnings, but the company’s artificial-intelligence labs are generating losses that fully offset the cloud profit, highlighting the financial strain of its AI investments.

headline: Conservatives select James Cleverly as London mayor candidate
summary: Former home secretary James Cleverly won 86% of the vote among London Tory members to become the Conservative candidate for the 2028 mayoral election, pledging to challenge “anti-London” policies.

headline: Western allies gather in Berlin to back Ukraine
summary: Germany hosts 40 delegations showing solidarity for Kyiv as leaders of Russia, China and the United States meet in Shenzhen, underscoring heightened geopolitical tensions.

headline: Florida pastor convicted in Haitian president assassination plot
summary: Pastor Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty of involvement in the plot that led to the killing of Haiti’s former president Jovenel Moïse.

headline: Democrats divided despite midterm victories
summary: After securing control of Congress, Democratic leaders met in Denver, expressing frustration over internal splits and debating the party’s future direction.

headline: AFL draft night delivers tears for rookie and top pick Cochrane
summary: Essendon’s Archie Elliott broke down in tears after being selected at pick 17, having attended the night to support a friend. Meanwhile, Port Adelaide secured No 1 pick Dougie Cochrane, who welcomed the pressure of filling the void left by Zak Butters.

headline: Indian truck driver wins $1.3 million Diwali lottery
summary: A truck driver from Punjab, India, won a Diwali lottery prize worth $1.3 million, changing his fortunes overnight.

headline: Panmure Liberum strategist Joachim Klement exits personal stock holdings
summary: Market commentator Joachim Klement of Panmure Liberum has sold all of his personal stock positions, ending a long-standing fully-invested portfolio.

headline: Productivity Commission says climate and gender rules cost economy over $1 billion
summary: Australia’s Productivity Commission warned that compliance with new climate and gender-related regulations imposes more than $1 billion in annual costs, eroding economic productivity.

headline: Nvidia approaches Arm chief Rene Haas for potential CEO role
summary: Nvidia has reportedly reached out to Arm’s chief executive Rene Haas as a leading candidate to replace founder Jensen Huang as CEO, according to recruiting firm Heidrick & Struggles.

headline: NSW opposition leader Mark Speakman to quit seat ahead of election
summary: Mark Speakman announced he will not re-contest his Cronulla seat at the upcoming state election, joining a wave of Liberal departures under new leader Kellie Sloane.

headline: South Africa moves to replant five historic baobab trees
summary: Environmental groups are racing to replant five centuries-old baobab trees after an exporter attempted to ship them illegally to Georgia. The trees, rescued from a Durban warehouse, have been placed in a reserve in Timbavati and will be supported by cables to aid recovery.

headline: FIFA names challengers for Infantino’s 2027 presidential election
summary: The governing body of world football announced that former FIFA officials Diallo and Tashima will contest the 2027 presidential election, marking the first time incumbent Gianni Infantino will face an opponent after running unopposed in 2023.

headline: South African DJ featured in Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack
summary: Renowned South African electronic music producer DJ Lag will appear on the soundtrack of the upcoming video-game Grand Theft Auto 6, joining a roster of African artists highlighted in the game’s release.

headline: Police officer recounts fatal shooting of armed teenager
summary: A police officer who shot a 16-year-old boy said he feared for his life after the teenager approached with a knife. The officer’s testimony detailed the circumstances surrounding the fatal incident.

headline: Bond yields rise globally except in China
summary: Across major markets, bond yields are climbing, signalling higher borrowing costs, while China’s central bank has cut rates, keeping its yields lower than elsewhere. The divergence highlights differing monetary policy paths.

headline: Five teenagers charged after drive-by shooting raid
summary: Police raids led to the arrest of five 16-year-olds charged with the murder of Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau following a fatal drive-by shooting. The suspects remain in custody.

headline: Europe tightens, US eases sanctions on Russia
summary: European nations are strengthening sanctions against Russia, while the United States is rolling back some measures. The contrasting approaches reflect divergent strategies among Western allies in dealing with Moscow.

headline: AI poised to transform economics, warns The Economist
summary: The Economist argues that artificial intelligence is rapidly mastering mathematics and could soon disrupt the field of economics, raising concerns about future academic and policy impacts.

headline: Royal tour menus become focal point of criticism
summary: Media commentary highlighted the significance of menu choices during recent royal tours, noting that even minor culinary decisions can attract public scrutiny.

headline: Novartis lifts blockbuster drug sales forecasts
summary: Novartis raised its peak sales forecasts for several blockbuster medicines, citing strong demand for treatments in multiple sclerosis, leukemia and cholesterol, bringing the projected revenue to $18 billion.

headline: Former minister Sharman Stone dies aged 75
summary: Former Liberal minister and pioneering public servant Sharman Stone died at 75 after a long battle with brain cancer, choosing voluntary assisted dying.

headline: Air strike hits Saudi sovereign wealth fund headquarters
summary: An air strike targeted the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, the sovereign wealth fund, amid near-daily attacks by Houthi rebels on the kingdom.

headline: Uganda landslide survivors demand UN justice
summary: Survivors of a deadly landslide in Uganda have taken their case to the United Nations, rejecting relocation plans they say ignore safety, land rights and livelihoods.

headline: Dozens missing after migrant boat sinks off Senegal
summary: A boat carrying around 100 migrants sank off Senegal’s coast, leaving dozens missing and at least four bodies recovered, according to local media reports.

headline: Anthropic IPO could make employees multimillionaires
summary: Anthropic’s initial public offering today could value the average employee at over $40 million, according to SEC filings and investor estimates, potentially creating thousands of multimillion-dollar shareholders.

headline: Housing and retail risks raise recession fears
summary: Analysts warn that a shake-out in the housing and retail sectors could tip the Australian economy into recession, noting rising risks in official data and corporate job cuts.

headline: NASA expert explains physics behind Sandpapergate
summary: A NASA aerodynamics specialist detailed the scientific principles that made sandpaper an effective tool in the Sandpapergate cricket scandal involving former Test player Cameron Bancroft.

headline: Kimberley man sentenced to 10 years for partner’s death
summary: The Supreme Court sentenced Craig Charlton Rastus to ten years in prison for violently assaulting and killing his partner over a half-hour period in Mowanjum, Western Australia.

headline: Sydney aquatic centre redevelopment scrapped after $12.7m cost blowout
summary: The popular Sydney pool, closed since 2024, will not be rebuilt after a $12.7 million cost overrun forced the council to abandon the planned redevelopment. Officials said the financial gap made the project untenable, leaving the community without a key recreational facility.

headline: Sandpapergate scandal threatens Cummins' advertising spend
summary: Cummins faces potential loss of advertising revenue as sponsors reconsider backing the player at the centre of the Sandpapergate controversy. Companies that invested millions in marketing deals are now evaluating whether to continue association amid the growing backlash.

headline: Netflix drama portrays FTX collapse as toxic love story
summary: The Netflix series ‘The Altruists’ frames the $12 billion downfall of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX exchange as a destructive love story between two reckless crypto enthusiasts, shifting the narrative from corporate crime to personal tragedy.

headline: Busselton four-bed home listed at $2,300 weekly sparks outrage
summary: A four-bedroom, two-bathroom house in Busselton was advertised for $2,300 a week, prompting criticism from locals who say the price is unaffordable. The agent defended the rate, describing the property as a premium offering.

headline: Award-winning biography revives forgotten Australian author Elizabeth Harrower
summary: Susan Wyndham’s newly awarded biography brings back into focus the life of Elizabeth Harrower, an Australian writer praised by Patrick White who withdrew from public view in the 1970s. The book re-establishes her significance in the nation’s literary history.

headline: Penny Wong sanctions Israeli settlement actors, prompting ambassador's protest
summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong announced sanctions on several entities involved in illegal Israeli settlements. Israel’s ambassador responded with a strongly worded statement, accusing Canberra of ‘megaphone diplomacy’ over the new measures.

headline: Kenyan marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir banned for doping
summary: Four-time World Marathon Major winner Peres Jepchirchir has been stripped of her Sydney Marathon title and banned for three years after testing positive for EPO in an out-of-competition test.

headline: Labor touts low unemployment amid high inflation concerns
summary: The government highlights low unemployment as its biggest achievement, while facing entrenched high inflation and warnings of a potential surge in the jobless rate.

headline: Mother and stepfather charged in Gold Coast girl’s death
summary: Police have charged a mother and her partner with the alleged murder of 12-year-old Tiffani Scholten, who was found unresponsive at her Gold Coast home in 2022.

headline: Two men charged after theft of four Melbourne Cups and a Caulfield Cup
summary: Court proceedings revealed two men have been charged with stealing four Melbourne Cup trophies and a Caulfield Cup from racecourses in Melbourne.

headline: Music industry opposes Labor’s AI licensing carve-out
summary: ARIA chief Annabelle Herd and other creatives reject the Labor government’s proposed AI copyright carve-out, saying musicians stand with fellow creators against the plan.

headline: Eyre Peninsula schools to close as transmission line repair takes days
summary: South Australia warned that repairing the main electricity transmission line to the Eyre Peninsula could take several days, prompting the activation of backup generators and temporary school closures across the region.

headline: Violent protests erupt in Bangladesh ahead of Sheikh Hasina’s planned return
summary: Bangladesh saw clashes, bomb blasts and arson as supporters of exiled former prime minister Sheikh Hasina staged nationwide protests after the government rejected her passport request, with parts of the country shut down and the home of Muhammad Yunus set alight.

headline: Humm appoints new company secretary amid regulatory scrutiny
summary: Humm has named a new company secretary, a move that highlights ongoing governance challenges at the fintech firm, which has faced a series of regulatory issues in recent months.

headline: Gold Coast council evicts homeless man for Father's Day picnic
summary: The City of Gold Coast removed a homeless man from a public area to make way for a Father's Day picnic event, sparking criticism of the council’s handling of the situation.

headline: Big Build royal commission refers two witnesses for possible prosecution
summary: The Big Build royal commission has referred former Bandidos member Joel Leavitt and labour-hire boss Bernard Kearney to authorities over allegations they failed to answer the commission’s questions.

headline: WA fishing council urges industry unity to prevent further decline
summary: Following the demersal fishing inquiry, the Western Australian Fishing Industry Council has refreshed its board and warned that the sector must unite to avoid additional shrinkage amid ongoing challenges.

headline: APEC summit hosts historic US-China-Russia talks as Albanese urges peace
summary: At the 2026 APEC summit in Shenzhen, leaders of the United States, China and Russia held a three-way meeting, while Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese appealed to Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine.

headline: Midwife warned Hunter mum against twins homebirth before fatal infection
summary: A midwife testified at a Hunter family inquest that she warned the mother against a homebirth with twins due to infection risk. She said she urged hospital delivery, but the babies later died from a fatal infection, prompting calls for review of homebirth guidance.

headline: Darwin Port lease dispute deepens as Landbridge vows legal action
summary: The Australian government and Chinese-owned Landbridge Ltd remain at odds over the lease of the Darwin Port. Prime Minister Albanese says talks are ongoing, while Landbridge denies any settlement and says it will continue legal action to protect its interests.

headline: Goodman shareholders strike over proposed data centre build
summary: Shareholders of Goodman Group staged a walk-out at the annual general meeting, protesting the company’s plan to build a large data centre. The protest marks the sixth activist action against Goodman, highlighting tension between its growth ambitions and concerns over environmental and community impacts.

headline: Bugs bassist Jordan Brunoli dies aged 31 after cancer battle
summary: Jordan Brunoli, 31, bassist for Australian rock band Bugs, died in Brisbane after a battle with cancer. He was surrounded by family and friends at the time of his passing, prompting tributes from fellow musicians and fans across the country.

headline: Security watchdog proposes dropping ‘religion’ from terrorism definition
summary: The Australian National Security Committee has proposed removing the word “religion” from the legal definition of terrorism. The change aims to simplify prosecutions and focus on violent intent, with supporters saying it will aid law-enforcement while critics warn it could narrow the scope of terrorism offences.

headline: Direct cremations now account for one in five funerals
summary: The 2026 Cost of Dying Report shows that direct cremation has become the choice for about 20% of funerals, a rise attributed to changes in preferences since the pandemic.

headline: Queensland caravan firm enters voluntary liquidation, customers lose deposits
summary: A Queensland caravan company has gone into voluntary liquidation, leaving customers without their pre-Christmas deposits and uncertain about delivery of their orders.

headline: Inquest finds preventable death of Aboriginal woman in NSW prison
summary: A coroner’s inquest concluded that the death of 47-year-old Tammy Shipley in a NSW women’s prison was preventable, citing failures to monitor her excessive water consumption as required.

headline: NSW inquest hears mother ignored advice, twins homebirth leads to infant death
summary: An NSW inquest heard that a mother refused hospital birth for her twins after hearing traumatic stories, resulting in the death of one baby despite expert warnings.

headline: Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus banned from Dublin match, hosts online watch-along
summary: Rassie Erasmus has been barred from the Springboks’ clash with Ireland in Dublin and will instead host supporters for an online watch-along from his hotel.

headline: Fund managers cheer removal of legal overhang after Count court win
summary: Bankers say the legal dispute surrounding Count’s court win has cleared a major overhang on the share price, boosting confidence among fund managers.

headline: Elon Musk says Ukrainian president not always truthful about Starshield
summary: Elon Musk told reporters that Ukrainian President Zelenskyy’s statements about restrictions on the Starshield network are not always truthful.

headline: Leftover pumpkins used to provide thousandth free meal
summary: A sustainable food organisation has turned surplus pumpkins into the 1,000th free meal, helping people facing tough times.

headline: Victorian businesses complain of rising taxes, expenses, say ‘nothing left’
summary: Small and medium-sized businesses in Victoria say they are fed up with increasing taxes and costs, describing the situation as leaving ‘nothing left’ for them.

headline: Tasmanian road safety council urges seatbelt use after 831 offences
summary: The Road Safety Advisory Council warns that 831 seatbelt offences in a year show many Tasmanians still risk themselves and others by not wearing seatbelts correctly.

headline: Labor staff occupy Qantas chairman’s lounge for trans-continental travel event
summary: Members of the Labor party filled the Qantas Chairman’s Lounge, turning it into a venue for an international travel-focused gathering.

headline: AI telemarketer ‘Alex’ pressures Australians to switch super funds
summary: The AI bot ‘Alex’ mimics a bored telemarketer, urging listeners to move their superannuation to other providers and seeking personal financial information.

headline: Aboriginal artist wins ARIA, urges voters to consider choices
summary: An Aboriginal musician accepted an ARIA award and used the platform to call on voters to think carefully about their electoral decisions.

headline: Global survey finds flexibility outweighs pay as top reason workers consider leaving
summary: A poll of over 40,000 workers worldwide shows that better work-life balance and flexible schedules are now the main factors prompting people to look for new jobs, ahead of higher salaries.

headline: One Nation revises migration policy amid criticism
summary: One Nation removed its previous migration platform from its website and announced a new policy at a press conference, marking the third iteration of its stance. Critics say the changes mask billionaire interests and betray working-class voters, while internal disagreements persist over target arrival numbers.

headline: Wreck of Australia’s first locally built warship found
summary: Marine archaeologists have located the remains of the HMCS Spitfire, Australia’s first domestically built warship, off far north Queensland. The discovery coincides with the 128th anniversary of its sinking in 1898, offering new insights into colonial naval history.

headline: Christmas Island red crabs begin annual migration
summary: The iconic red crabs of Christmas Island have started their yearly migration, a key ecological event that supports the island’s ecosystem. Authorities are monitoring the movement as the crabs travel from forest to sea to breed.

headline: Weight-loss drugs used in nearly one in ten UK households
summary: A survey finds that 8.5% of households in Great Britain contain at least one person taking GLP-1 weight-loss medication, with about 2.6 million adults using the drugs in August, a rise of roughly 700,000 since February.

headline: IEA warns global data-centre power demand could double by 2030
summary: The International Energy Agency says electricity use by data centres worldwide could double by 2030 as AI workloads increase pressure on power grids.

headline: US manufacturers accelerate robot adoption to address labour shortage
summary: Companies are increasing automation to mitigate workforce gaps, though experts say the pace remains insufficient for the sector to stay internationally competitive as manufacturing struggles.

headline: Retail investors face squeeze ahead of major IPO
summary: A surge in demand for AI-related stocks is testing Wall Street’s capacity to accommodate a growing wave of individual investors, raising concerns about pricing and allocation in upcoming blockbuster IPOs.

headline: US housing shortage hampers labour mobility
summary: Analysts say America’s inadequate supply of homes is preventing workers from moving to regions with better job prospects, intensifying pressure on the housing market and broader economy.

headline: Gold loses appeal as safe-haven amid tech stock decline
summary: Investors are turning away from gold, which has failed to provide portfolio protection during recent falls in technology stocks, reducing its attractiveness as a diversifier.

headline: Adani empire expands after legal battles, strengthens ties to Modi
summary: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani has turned around a period of lawsuits and fraud accusations, now overseeing a vastly larger business group that benefits from close relations with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, boosting its influence across sectors.

headline: UK faces obstacles to rejoining EU despite renewed overtures
summary: The United Kingdom has signalled interest in restoring its pre-Brexit relationship with the European Union, but legal, economic and political complexities mean a full return to EU membership is unlikely in the near term.

headline: Xi meeting marks diplomatic milestone but raises concerns
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s recent high-profile meeting is hailed as a significant diplomatic achievement, yet analysts note that unresolved issues and Xi’s reluctance to discuss certain topics with leaders such as Putin and Trump could limit its impact.

headline: Low-cost Chinese EVs depress Australian used-car prices
summary: In Australia, inexpensive electric vehicles imported from China are driving down resale values of petrol and diesel cars, with some models losing up to five times their previous worth, prompting concerns that traditional vehicles may become hard to sell.

headline: Ash Barty to be inducted into International Tennis Hall of Fame
summary: Australian tennis champion Ash Barty has been told she will be inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame. The 28-year-old, who retired in 2022, said she feels humbled and uncertain about the honour, but the induction recognises her Grand Slam victories and world-number-one status.

headline: Apprentice jockey Siena Grima eyes feature race after missing Group 1 win
summary: Siena Grima, who missed a chance at the $1 million Gong Group 1 race, hopes to capitalize on a long-shot start in an upcoming feature race.

headline: UN report finds one in four women cannot refuse sex in marriage
summary: A United Nations Population Fund report reveals that 25% of women worldwide lack the ability to refuse sex when a partner demands it. The highest rates are in West and Central Africa, where 45% of women cannot say no, with lower but still significant figures in East and Southern Africa, Arab states and Latin America.

headline: Beau Lamarre-Condon double-murder trial reaches closing addresses
summary: The trial of former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon for a double murder entered its final phase as the Crown prosecutor and defence presented closing arguments before jury deliberations.

headline: Perth schools commit to pay $300k foreshore pledge from 2024
summary: Wesley College and Penrhos College will honour their $300,000 commitment to a South Perth foreshore project, after the council alleged the schools had reneged on the promise.

headline: Gulag survivor argues superpower summits won’t decide Ukraine’s fate
summary: A former gulag prisoner writing from Lviv contended that meetings of leaders like Trump, Xi and Putin cannot determine Ukraine’s future, emphasizing the need for broader international engagement.

headline: Amplia Therapeutics cleared for pancreatic cancer trial
summary: Amplia Therapeutics received ethics approval for its ACCENT-Mini trial, which will test daily doses of narmafotinib alongside chemotherapy in patients with pancreatic cancer.

headline: Korean media, gaming and travel stocks surge on China deal hopes
summary: Shares of South Korean media, gaming and travel companies jumped after investors priced in the possibility of expanded access to the Chinese market under a new trade agreement.

headline: Unemployment rises to five-year high, hinting recession risk
summary: Australia's jobless rate climbed to 4.9% in October, up from 4.7%, as the labour market shed 43,500 jobs. The jump adds to concerns that five interest-rate hikes have pushed the economy toward a recession, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

headline: Dalaroo Metals begins drilling at high-grade gold find in Ivory Coast
summary: Dalaroo Metals has started a diamond-drilling program at its 18-metre, 7.31 g/t gold intercept in Côte d’Ivoire, targeting a 20,000-metre campaign to delineate the deposit.

headline: Meta pauses plan for non-voting share class after lawsuit
summary: Meta has halted its proposal to create a non-voting share class that would let founder Mark Zuckerberg sell shares without diluting control, following a shareholder lawsuit challenging the move.

headline: One Nation candidate’s migrant welfare graph called inaccurate
summary: Researcher criticised One Nation candidate Katherine Deves for using a graph that misrepresents welfare rates by country of birth to argue for stricter migration cuts.

headline: Sandpapergate fallout: former player speaks, critics warn political impact
summary: Former Australia opening batter Cameron Bancroft broke his silence on the 2018 sandpaper scandal, while former Cricket Australia staffer Kate Hutchison recounted her attempts to raise concerns, prompting debate over the episode's broader political ramifications.

headline: Hippo under constant medical watch after swallowing hat
summary: A hippo at a U.S. zoo is being closely monitored after it accidentally ingested a hat thrown into its enclosure, prompting round-the-clock veterinary care.

headline: Larrimah Hotel in NT back on market for third time
summary: The Pink Panther pub in Larrimah, Northern Territory, which became linked to the 2017 disappearance of Paddy Moriarty and his dog, is up for sale again, marking its third listing since the mystery began.

headline: 88-year-old man found unfit to plead to wife’s murder
summary: Canberra man Manfred Uhle, 88, charged with repeatedly stabbing his 78-year-old wife, was deemed unfit to plead during a special court hearing, meaning he is likely to spend life in custody.

headline: WA Wheatbelt community mourns three friends killed in crash
summary: The deaths of Jarvis Noakes, Jake McKay and Isabel Garnett in a vehicle crash in Western Australia’s Wheatbelt have prompted an outpouring of tributes and grief across the Narrogin community.

headline: Five arrested in Logan homicide investigation
summary: Police raids in Queensland led to the arrest of five people linked to a fatal shooting that occurred in Logan last month, as part of an ongoing homicide probe.

headline: Jardines considers launching first private-equity fund
summary: Hong Kong-based conglomerate Jardines, with a 194-year history, is weighing the creation of its inaugural private-equity fund as it shifts from operating businesses to an investment-focused model.

headline: Ellerston Capital writes off stake in TikTok-used video firm
summary: Early investor Ellerston Capital has written off its holding in a video-technology company that supplies platforms such as TikTok and Canva, citing the firm’s new capital structure and shareholder decisions.

headline: State tribunal rejects North Stoneville 1,001-lot development plan
summary: The State Administrative Tribunal dismissed land developer Satterley’s appeal, confirming the rejection of its proposal to build a 1,001-lot town for 2,800 residents on a 535-hectare site in North Stoneville.

headline: Cruise lines pull out of Australia, industry loses $1.75 billion
summary: Major international cruise operators are abandoning the Australian market, wiping more than $1 billion from the sector’s contribution to the economy and signalling a sharp decline in cruise-related tourism revenue.

headline: Labor campaign architect offers strategic advice to NSW leaders
summary: A key strategist behind Labor’s successful state campaigns shared insights and recommendations with party leaders in New South Wales, suggesting the Victorian contest is largely decided but emphasizing remaining opportunities.

headline: Elon Musk calls US midterm spending ‘pretty foolish’
summary: Elon Musk said the record spending on the United States midterm elections was “pretty foolish” and distanced himself from the MAGA movement, while also praising Nvidia’s Jensen Huang as irreplaceable.

headline: Surfing duo Pride aim to improve Kembla performance
summary: Joe Pride, after securing second place in two Kembla surf features last year, believes he and his partner can challenge for better results in the upcoming Saturday event.

headline: Wallabies aim to revive attack against Wales
summary: The Australian rugby union side says it will adopt a more polished attacking approach in its upcoming test against in-form Wales, hoping to halt an eight-match losing streak in Europe.

headline: Star 350 times larger than Sun observed devouring neighbour
summary: Astronomers have directly captured a massive star, 350 times the Sun’s size, in the act of consuming a nearby companion, a phenomenon previously only inferred.

headline: Forster’s novel adapted for Southbank Theatre
summary: A new production of E.M. Forster’s 1908 novel arrives at Southbank Theatre, offering a contemporary take that blends the original story’s themes of freedom and sexual awakening with modern staging.

headline: Cameron Munster to explore Sydney club offers
summary: Veteran NRL playmaker Cameron Munster will meet interested Sydney clubs to assess his market value, despite a reduced contract offer from the Storm.

headline: Jake Ireland named 2026 Stawell Gift winner after drug scandal
summary: Following the disqualification of original winner Olufemi Komolafe for testing positive to ADHD medication, Jake Ireland has been declared the new champion of the 2026 Stawell Gift.

headline: One Nation faces internal turmoil amid leaks and leadership interview
summary: One Nation’s newly appointed general manager Kelvin Morton has taken leave amid speculation of sidelining after a series of leaks, while party leader Warren Pickering discusses his favourite author and dream dinner guest in a rapid-fire interview.

headline: Mid-tier accounting firms surge as big four contract
summary: Australia’s top 100 accounting firms posted a 3 per cent revenue rise to $15.6 billion, driven by growth in mid-tier firms even as Deloitte, EY, KPMG and PwC trimmed staff and revenue.

headline: Tasmanian premier rejects data-centre moratorium
summary: The Tasmanian government has refused to adopt a non-binding motion passed in the lower house that called for a halt to new data-centre projects, saying it would grind the state’s economy to a halt.

headline: Worley chairman John Grill to step down after five decades
summary: Global engineering firm Worley announced that founder and chairman John Grill will exit his leadership role next year, ending more than 50 years of senior involvement with the company.

headline: Super switching advice should focus on investment ethos
summary: Industry analysts say Australians’ growing super balances require advice that prioritises investment philosophy over product labels, reflecting diverse needs rather than systemic failure.

headline: Anthropic valued up to $1.5tn ahead of market debut
summary: AI start-up Anthropic, founded five years ago, is now valued at up to $1.5 trillion as it prepares for a potential stock market listing, making it one of the world’s biggest artificial-intelligence firms.

headline: Elon Musk says he feels foolish after $500mn Republican donation
summary: SpaceX chief Elon Musk said he feels “foolish” after donating nearly $500 million to Republican candidates, acknowledging the money failed to influence the mid-term election outcome.

headline: Aurum Resources reports new gold hits at Ivory Coast Boundiali project
summary: Aurum Resources announced further gold intercepts at its 3.84 Moz Boundiali project in Côte d’Ivoire, extending the deposit’s depth potential across several stacked lodes.

headline: Sarytogan signs MOU to supply graphite for Kazakhstan battery plant
summary: Sarytogan Graphite has signed a memorandum of understanding to provide graphite for a planned one-GWh battery-cell factory in Kazakhstan, positioning its deposit as a key local supplier.

headline: Cortisol-blocking pill shows benefit for older dementia patients
summary: A daily drug that blocks cortisol did not help all Alzheimer’s patients in a pivotal trial, but it showed a positive effect for older participants with dementia.

headline: Regional Arts Triennial showcases hope and connection
summary: The third Regional Arts Triennial, titled “Radical Futures”, displays works that explore how artists can act as catalysts for change during uncertain times.

headline: AFL draft dates and process explained for aspiring players
summary: The AFL draft has arrived, offering dozens of teenage footballers a chance to be selected; the guide outlines when it takes place and how the system works.

headline: Five men arrested after fatal drive-by shooting at Queensland pub
summary: Police arrested five men following a drive-by shooting at a Queensland pub that killed a 19-year-old woman and injured three men.

headline: Bancroft claims freedom as Cummins faces captaincy questions
summary: Former Australian cricketer Cameron Bancroft said he feels “freed” after his allegations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, prompting concerns for captain Pat Cummins and the national team’s coaching staff.

headline: Traders expect RBA to hold rates, eye early cut after weak jobs data
summary: Weak jobs data has led bond traders to price in a small chance of an RBA rate cut as early as February, reinforcing expectations that the central bank will not hike again soon.

headline: Former PwC partner receives five-year ban for falsifying tax documents

summary: Lowe's said online sales were strong during the quarter and upgraded its full-year outlook despite a sluggish housing market.

headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in historic China summit
summary: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin will gather in China for a first-ever trilateral summit on Thursday, marking a rare high-level meeting of the three leaders.

headline: Gloucester Cathedral restructures amid significant financial pressure
summary: Staff at Gloucester Cathedral are undergoing a review as the historic institution implements a restructure to address mounting financial challenges.

headline: Fed Governor Waller says rate hikes may be needed to shock inflation
summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller warned that the central bank could need to raise rates sharply, possibly by a full percentage point, to bring inflation back to target after it lingered above 2%. He said a more aggressive stance may be required to cool price pressures.

headline: Critics hail Grand Theft Auto 6 as a masterpiece
summary: Reviewers have praised Grand Theft Auto 6, calling it the most anticipated video game to live up to its hype and describing it as a masterpiece.

headline: Only Alphabet and Apple beat the S&P 500 among Magnificent Seven stocks
summary: Since the start of 2025, just two of the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks, Alphabet and Apple, have outperformed the S&P 500, reflecting varied success in AI-driven strategies.

headline: William and Kate meet Indian Prime Minister Modi in New Delhi
summary: During a surprise addition to their India tour, the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, following their appearance at the Earthshot Prize ceremony.

headline: Housing market outlook bleak as sales slump and mortgage demand drops
summary: Two new reports highlighted a worsening housing market, citing record-low sales and high mortgage rates. Mortgage demand fell sharply as rates rose to their highest level in three weeks, signalling reduced activity for both refinances and new home purchases.

headline: US rules threaten Southeast Asia data-centre boom built on Chinese demand
summary: New U.S. regulations requiring approval for advanced AI chip purchases could slow the rapid expansion of data centres in Southeast Asia, a sector that has grown largely on Chinese demand.

headline: Jim Cramer lists top ten market watch items for Wednesday
summary: Jim Cramer highlighted ten key points to watch in the market, questioning whether Nvidia can sustain its recent gains after its earnings report.

headline: AI power scramble: which companies stand to profit the most
summary: Analysts examine the rush among big tech firms to secure AI partnerships with traditional power companies, urging investors to look beyond headlines to identify genuine profit opportunities.

headline: Israel delays West Bank settlement contracts after UK sanctions
summary: Israel postponed issuing building contracts for a large West Bank settlement, days after the UK imposed sanctions on firms involved in the project, with officials saying the decision should await a new caretaker government.

headline: Hims & Hers adds unapproved peptide treatments
summary: Telehealth provider Hims & Hers announced a new line of compounded peptide products, including sermorelin and NAD+, despite none being approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

headline: Australian wages post strongest quarterly rise in two years
summary: Private-sector wages grew 1.0% in the September quarter, giving an annual increase of 3.4%, the highest rate in two years. Despite the rise, real wages fell, leaving workers still lagging behind inflation and highlighting ongoing cost-of-living pressures.

headline: Business groups plan own productivity summit as hope fades in government reforms
summary: Around 30 business and industry bodies are organising a summit to discuss ways to boost Australian productivity, citing disappointment with the government's reform agenda and calling for tax cuts and other measures to improve efficiency.

headline: Research finds Business Council of Australia backs gas expansion contrary to member climate views
summary: InfluenceMap analysis shows the Business Council of Australia is lobbying for new gas supply projects, a stance that conflicts with the climate concerns expressed by most of its member companies, and the council does not disclose its energy and climate committee members.

headline: One Nation claims Australia’s refugee program is second-largest
summary: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson argued that Australia’s refugee scheme ranks second globally, using the claim to justify a proposed 90 % cut to the annual intake of 20,000 places.

headline: U.S. soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
summary: A senior U.S. serviceman was taken into military custody in the United Kingdom after being suspected of espionage and other national-security offences on behalf of Russia.

headline: Investors advised on AI-bubble risk and diversification
summary: With AI stocks showing heightened volatility, market experts recommend diversifying portfolios while maintaining long-term exposure, suggesting a balanced approach to mitigate potential bubble fallout.

headline: Kuwait says it repelled Iranian attack after US strike
summary: Kuwait reported that it successfully defended against its first Iranian attack in two months, following a US air strike on Iran’s Qeshm island, with Bahrain also claiming to have been hit.

headline: Telstra outage prompts surge in consumer complaints
summary: Following recent mobile and internet outages, Telstra customers are increasingly lodging complaints and compensation claims with the industry ombudsman, with consumer groups urging automatic compensation for affected users.

headline: Paris Hilton backs AI deep-fake pornography legislation
summary: Actress Paris Hilton, supported by Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, is lobbying for the Defiance Act, which aims to criminalise AI-generated deep-fake pornography, after its passage in the US Senate.

headline: Booking Holdings launches AI-driven enterprise travel division
summary: Online travel giant Booking Holdings announced a new business-to-business division focused on using artificial intelligence to reshape corporate travel planning and improve platform scalability.

headline: IEA chief says Strait of Hormuz confidence shattered
summary: The International Energy Agency’s chief warned that the war in Ukraine has crushed confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable energy corridor, stating there is no credible pathway back to pre-war normality for shipping through the strategic waterway.

headline: Harry Styles, Billie Eilish, Cher to headline Glastonbury 2027
summary: The line-up for the UK’s Glastonbury Festival in June 2027 has been revealed, with pop star Harry Styles, singer-songwriter Billie Eilish and legendary performer Cher confirmed as headliners among other acts.

headline: Bancroft alleges team knew of 2018 sandpaper plot
summary: Former Australian Test batsman Cameron Bancroft claimed in a 4,000-word statement that the entire Australian cricket team was aware of the 2018 sandpaper cheating scheme, intensifying pressure on current captain Pat Cummins as new revelations emerge.

headline: Coalition urges national focus on classroom disruption
summary: The opposition coalition argued that Australia’s classrooms are among the most disrupted globally, citing a survey that found nine minutes of every half-hour are lost to misbehaviour, and called for calming measures to become a national priority.

headline: China’s military seeks Nvidia chips for AI projects
summary: A US congressional commission reported that China’s armed forces are pursuing Nvidia’s advanced graphics processors to boost artificial-intelligence capabilities, amid ongoing scrutiny of the chipmaker following its CEO’s resignation over alleged ties to a suspected Chinese spy.

headline: Cameron Green criticised for run-out decision
summary: Australia’s Cameron Green faced backlash after a controversial run-out of teammate Alex Carey during the test match against England, with commentators describing the decision as a ‘disgraceful’ error that cost the side momentum.

headline: Tame Impala makes ARIA history amid AI debate
summary: At the ARIA Awards, Tame Impala became the most awarded act, overtaking John Farnham, while artists voiced concerns that artificial intelligence threatens music originality, sparking a broader discussion about AI’s role in the industry.

headline: Democrats secure Alaska Senate seat as Mary Peltola declared winner
summary: Mary Peltola has been confirmed as the winner of the Alaska Senate race, giving Democrats another victory following the recent midterm elections and solidifying their control of the Senate.

headline: US may sanction ICJ judges after potential Myanmar genocide ruling
summary: Concerns are rising that the United States could impose sanctions on International Court of Justice judges, including Nobel laureate Navi Pillay, if the court issues a ruling that finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against the Rohingya.

headline: Democrats probe Cantor Fitzgerald's Nvidia ties in post-midterm congressional inquiry
summary: Following the Democratic sweep of the 2024 midterms, a House committee has launched a probe into Cantor Fitzgerald's business relationships with Nvidia, marking one of the first investigations under the new Democratic majority.

headline: Study alleges 'phantom forests' in arid Australia used for dubious carbon credits
summary: Researchers claim that regeneration projects in semi-arid parts of Australia have produced only minimal increases in forest cover, yet are being used to generate carbon credits that allow fossil-fuel companies to offset emissions, sparking a policy debate.

headline: British hacker sentenced to six years in US for $11 million text-message scam
summary: Tyler Buchanan, a Dundee-born member of the Scattered Spider hacking group, was sentenced in the United States to six years in prison for a text-message fraud scheme that stole $11 million.

headline: Ghanaian president’s $60 million jet purchase sparks public anger
summary: The acquisition of a new presidential jet costing $60 million has provoked widespread outrage in Ghana, where many citizens are facing rising living costs.

headline: Ben Duckett scores ODI century against Australia
summary: England opener Ben Duckett hit a hundred in the third One Day International in Hobart, leading his side to a strong position against the hosts.

headline: Top CEOs say AI skills key to productivity boost
summary: Chief executives of Wesfarmers, Origin Energy, Telstra and the Commonwealth Bank argue that investing in artificial-intelligence capabilities will unlock significant productivity gains for Australian businesses.

headline: Spender urges Chalmers to reconsider CGT reforms
summary: Independent senator Allegra Spender tells Treasury chief Jim Chalmers that the business sector, not government, best understands investment flows and should have a stronger voice in capital-gains-tax policy.

headline: Labor proposes AI carve-out for music licensing
summary: The government’s model would let AI developers such as Anthropic and OpenAI train on Australian music content only after paying for a permit, aiming to address artist concerns over copyright use.

headline: Gas reservation policy criticised for mixed signals
summary: Analysts say the proposed national gas reservation scheme sends contradictory messages and leaves outcomes uncertain, questioning its effectiveness in stabilising energy prices.

headline: Royal Albo’s faces scrutiny over $6 million federal grant
summary: Members of the Royal Albo’s golf club worry about the $6 million Commonwealth funding they secured, amid concerns about the club’s financial management and political optics.

headline: MONA’s losses top $500 million, founder remains optimistic
summary: The Museum of Old and New Art in Hobart reports accumulated deficits exceeding half a billion dollars, but founder David Walsh says the institution is on track to return to profitability.

headline: Foreign buyers flood Australian small-cap market
summary: Takeover bids surge as overseas investors target Australia’s overlooked small-cap companies, while private-equity firms capitalise on the sector’s five-year low valuations and potential rebound in industrial and property stocks.

headline: McGrath family farm cited in carbon-offset controversy
summary: A scientific study highlights the farm owned by former fast-bowler Glenn McGrath’s brother as an example of questionable carbon-offset projects worth millions of dollars.

headline: MP calls for faster heating-oil payments in Northumberland
summary: Around 23,000 households relying on heating oil face rising winter bills, prompting a local MP to urge the council to accelerate subsidy payments.

summary: Democrats secured the Alaska Senate race, delivering the party’s strongest mid-term performance since 1958. The contest concluded after legal disputes involving two candidates named Dan Sullivan, with the Democratic victor defeating the Republican opponent to claim the seat.

headline: David Jones to cut over 1,500 jobs as receiver closes stores
summary: The retailer’s receiver plans to shut half of David Jones’ department-store network, resulting in more than 1,500 job losses, many of which are casual positions without entitlements, as the company restructures under administration.

headline: Federal government adds $20 million to Darwin aged-care project
summary: The Commonwealth has increased funding for a planned aged-care centre in Palmerston, a satellite city of Darwin, by $20 million, allowing an additional 30 beds to be built and accelerating the project’s timeline.

headline: Byron Bay doula accused of abandoning newborn during inflating castle, inquest hears
summary: An inquest into a newborn’s death near Byron Bay heard that a doula left the infant unattended to inflate a jumping castle after the baby turned purple, raising serious concerns about untrained birth assistance.

headline: England clinches ODI series as Australia falters
summary: England won the one-day international series after Australia collapsed in the chase, despite a century from Ben Duckett. Cameron Green left the field after a bouncer struck his helmet, contributing to the home side’s defeat in Hobart.

headline: Family First disendorses candidate over unacceptable online posts
summary: Family First announced it is withdrawing its endorsement of a political candidate after discovering offensive material posted online, stating the party missed the content during its vetting process.

headline: Anthropic plans Nasdaq IPO as investor demand surges
summary: AI lab Anthropic is set to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT" on Thursday, with the company considering expanding the offering after strong investor interest.

summary: Victoria’s Big Build royal commission interrogated a Bandidos member about a $165,000 invoice for work on public projects, alleging he exploited the CFMEU’s influence and acted as a “bikie heavy”.

headline: NAB chief warns strict capital rules hinder Australian growth
summary: Andrew Irvine, chief executive of National Australia Bank, cautioned that Australia’s conservative bank-capital regulations may be stifling economic expansion, calling for a review of the risk-based framework.

summary: During a confirmation hearing, acting Navy secretary Hung Cao told senators the Navy has been using expired munitions as the Iran conflict strains weapons stocks and naval deployments, prompting concerns over readiness and costs.

headline: Iconic Australian piemaker Patties set for $1 billion-plus sale
summary: Morgan Stanley reports that Patties, once a local pie brand, is now a global manufacturer with a broadened product range and is expected to fetch over $1 billion in an upcoming auction.

summary: Tom Papley received a three-match suspension after a secondary sample from a roadside drug test confirmed the presence of cocaine and MDMA, prompting the AFL to enforce its anti-drug policy.

summary: Australian broadcaster Nine announced it will no longer air the Champions League, leaving fans to seek the competition on an international streaming service or its local subsidiary, potentially increasing subscription fees.

summary: In the deciding one-day international in Hobart, Australia needed 329 runs for victory as England were bowled out, with Edwards and Renshaw leading the chase.

headline: UK consumer price inflation rises to 3.6% in October
summary: The UK's annual CPI increased to 3.6% in October, driven by higher energy costs linked to the Middle East conflict, matching economists' forecasts.

headline: Around 60% of Victorian votes cast early in state election

headline: Labor's latest migration plan criticised as policy misstep
summary: Analysts say the government's recent migration reforms fail to balance political pressures with economic realities, labeling it a bungle.

headline: Voters prefer spending cuts over tax hikes to reduce deficit
summary: New polling indicates Australians want the government to address the budget deficit by reducing expenditure rather than increasing taxes.

headline: Canberra man charged after police chase, firearms seized

summary: A US private-equity firm has made an offer close to $1 billion to acquire software company Nuix, ending a turbulent six-year period for the firm.

headline: Trump's actions give China more reason to distrust the Quad
summary: Analysts argue that former US President Donald Trump's policies have increased Chinese antagonism toward the Quad partnership.

headline: Williamstown candidate confronts alleged vandal over corflutes
summary: A video shows political candidate Paul Lindemann chasing a person he claims defaced campaign signs in Williamstown.

summary: Two extremely rare conjoined twins born on a remote Papua New Guinea island died within weeks, prompting calls for improved medical referral pathways.

summary: ING announced a restructure of its global corporate and institutional division that will affect its Australian operations. The changes have not yet been approved, and the bank expects to begin a consultation process in the coming weeks.

summary: A patient took their own life in the bathroom of The Prince Charles Hospital’s mental health ward, Health Minister Tim Nicholls said in parliament. The incident adds to a cluster of three inpatient suicides at the hospital over the past seven months.

summary: A manager at a disability home was found to have accessed clients’ accounts and made 25 unauthorised transactions, stealing a total of $16,000. The case highlights concerns over financial safeguards for vulnerable Australians.

summary: Following the discovery of a skip-bin used to conceal the body of Melbourne Cup runner So You Are, jockey Rachel King expressed distress and the racing community is urging reforms to prevent similar incidents.

headline: Official trailer released for Australian black comedy ‘Bad Apples’
summary: The trailer for ‘Bad Apples’, starring Saoirse Ronan as a teacher dealing with a foul-mouthed troublemaker, has been released, generating buzz ahead of its Australian release.

headline: US Secretary of State says no link between recent tech outages
summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated there is “zero” evidence connecting recent technical failures at Microsoft, major banks, air-traffic control and the NSA, dismissing speculation about a coordinated attack.

headline: Robot fish feature in Powerhouse Museum’s summer festival
summary: An interactive reef installation with robot fish is part of five new productions at the Powerhouse Museum’s summer festival, designed to engage audiences ahead of the 2024 Olympics.

headline: Analysts see Nvidia earnings beat but warn of investor uncertainty
summary: Nvidia’s strong third-quarter results are expected to ease short-term concerns, yet analysts note lingering uncertainty about the company’s long-term leadership and market positioning.

summary: JPMorgan, together with Hyundai Card, is working on artificial-intelligence agents that can execute financial transactions without human involvement, signalling a push toward fully automated banking services.

headline: State legislators propose cut to social security contributions
summary: Deputies Gavin St Pier and Tom Rylatt have introduced an amendment to reduce social security contributions, prompting debate among state lawmakers over the fiscal impact of the proposal.

headline: Albanese urges China to lift beef tariffs ahead of APEC photo with Putin
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will press China to ease beef import duties while confirming he will join President Vladimir Putin for a joint photo at the APEC summit, a move drawing diplomatic attention.

headline: Sydney councils consider bans on smart glasses at beaches
summary: Local councils in Sydney are looking at restricting the use of smart glasses on popular beaches this summer, citing concerns over privacy and public safety as the emerging wearable technology becomes more widespread.

headline: Nearly 100 children potentially exposed to tuberculosis in Adelaide
summary: Health officials say almost 100 children attending a childcare centre in Adelaide may have been exposed to tuberculosis after a staff member tested positive for the disease, prompting contact tracing and testing measures.

headline: Broken Hill Gold to spin off Queensland assets into new $26.5m company
summary: Broken Hill Gold announced plans to separate its Queensland gold operations into a new listed entity, Manda Resources, valued at about $26.5 million, with a free share distribution to existing shareholders.

headline: Mother drowns while trying to rescue toddler in Melbourne lake
summary: A mother who attempted to save her toddler in a Melbourne lake drowned during the rescue attempt; the toddler also died in the incident.

headline: Victoria falls to bottom of national economic league table
summary: New data shows Victoria slipping to the lowest position among Australian states in the latest economic league table, undermining Premier Ben Carroll’s attempts to promote his government’s economic agenda.

headline: NSW announces tributes for first anniversary of Bondi shooting
summary: The New South Wales government has outlined a series of commemorative events to mark the first anniversary of the Bondi shooting, including memorial services and community outreach programmes.

summary: An Aboriginal mother claims a coach driver in Wagga Wagga asked her to leave the bus because her 22-month-old was crying, raising concerns about discrimination and public transport policies.

summary: England’s National Health Service has logged more than 3,000 cases of staff improperly accessing patients’ medical records over the past five years, prompting criticism from campaign groups and regulators over privacy breaches.

headline: Doula left newborn unattended to set up jumping castle
summary: A coronial inquest heard that a doula repeatedly told first-time parents their newborn was fine while the baby appeared purple and struggled to breathe, before leaving the infant to set up a jumping castle. The testimony has raised concerns about doula oversight and child safety.

summary: Leaked documents show Deutsche Bank appointed a member of a Qatari royal family, with internal papers indicating the hire blurred traditional lines between investor, client and counter-party. The move highlights the bank’s expanding ties to Gulf sovereign wealth and raises governance questions.
