summary: The recent disposal of the racehorse So You Are has shocked both the public and the racing sector. Industry bodies say no animal should be treated that way and promise stricter oversight to prevent similar incidents, amid calls for reform of animal-welfare standards.

headline: Two men break through Adelaide bank glass doors in brawl
summary: Police are seeking information after CCTV captured two men smashing through the glass entrance of a bank in Adelaide during a physical altercation. The incident, which caused significant property damage, is under investigation and officers have appealed for witnesses.

headline: WA child protection staffing still below needed levels
summary: Staffing in Western Australia’s Child Protection department remains inadequate, four years after the Pilbara murders of three children. Officials acknowledge gaps persist, with concerns that insufficient staff could affect the safety and welfare of vulnerable children across the state.

headline: Heritage trees on Canberra’s City Hill repeatedly set alight
summary: Police are investigating a series of arson incidents that have seen heritage-listed trees on City Hill in Canberra ignited multiple times over the past week. Authorities have not identified a suspect and are urging the public to report any information.

headline: Lendlease shares tumble to new low amid debt concerns
summary: Lendlease’s share price fell to a fresh low after Morgan Stanley warned of “deeper uncertainty” following the failure of a key asset sale. Investors are uneasy about the developer’s large debt load and the outlook for upcoming projects.

headline: Trial hears alleged murderer advised to erase phone data
summary: In South Australia’s Supreme Court, prosecutors say Liam Slann and his father received legal advice to wipe a phone after the 2024 killing of 21-year-old William Holdback. The jury is hearing details of the alleged murder and the advice given.

headline: Real wages fall for fourth straight quarter in Australia
summary: Australian real wages declined by 0.4% in the September quarter, marking the fourth consecutive decline. The report highlights which professions and jurisdictions performed better, underscoring ongoing pressure on household purchasing power.

headline: Chris Judd’s family fund posts poor performance after Melbourne Cup pick
summary: The Cerutty Macro Fund, managed by former AFL star Chris Judd and his wife, recorded a disappointing month, with the fund’s recent Melbourne Cup winner selection failing to boost returns. Analysts note the fund’s recent performance has been bleak.

headline: Larvotto secures US$30 million prepayment for NSW gold project
summary: Larvotto Resources received a US$30 million prepayment from partners Glencore and Wogen to support its gold-antimony ramp-up in New South Wales. The company also dispatched its first gold concentrate from the Hillgrove mine, marking a key production milestone.

headline: Critical security flaw discovered in Java programming language
summary: A tech start-up that previously uncovered a PHP vulnerability used AI tools to identify a serious bug in Java, the world’s third-largest programming language, raising concerns over potential exploitation by malicious actors.

headline: NSW government purchases outback station for future national park
summary: The New South Wales government bought a vast outback station that has been off-limits to traditional owners for 150 years, allowing the Malyangapa and Wilyakali peoples to access the land for the first time as plans for a national park progress.

headline: Labor outlines five key legislative battles before parliamentary year ends
summary: The government is focusing on five priority bills, including gas reservation reforms, a capital gains tax discount, and a digital duty of care. With the Coalition opposed and the Greens hesitant, Labor faces a tight timetable to secure support for its agenda.

headline: Iran says its army struck US drone and missile sites in Kuwait
summary: Iran announced that its armed forces targeted United States drone and missile installations at Kuwait’s Ali Al Salem air base, marking an escalation in a series of attacks on Gulf states amid heightened regional tensions.

headline: Alceon banker discussed potential deal with Bathla developer before collapse
summary: A confidential email reveals a senior Alceon banker talked about working with property developer Bathla over breakfast with the developer’s CEO weeks before Bathla’s financial collapse, highlighting early internal discussions about a possible partnership.

headline: US-backed mineral highway aims to boost Congo peace and prosperity
summary: The Lobito Corridor, a proposed transport route across the Democratic Republic of Congo, is at the centre of a United States-supported initiative to secure access to Africa’s critical minerals. Proponents say the project could foster economic development and stability in the region.

headline: One Nation proposes 90% cut to refugee intake and ends parent visas
summary: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson announced a plan to slash Australia’s refugee programme by 90% and abolish the permanent parent visa. The proposal drew swift criticism from opposition parties and refugee advocacy groups, who called it a cheap attack on vulnerable migrants.

headline: Putin urges Eurasian order ahead of meeting with Xi and Trump
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin delivered a rare address to global CEOs in China, calling for a new Eurasian order and criticizing Western powers, just before a high-profile summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and former US President Donald Trump.

headline: Students and teachers evacuated after school bus fire near Great Ocean Road
summary: A fire broke out on a school bus travelling near the Great Ocean Road. All passengers were safely evacuated, and local farmers assisted firefighters by supplying water tankers to help control the blaze.

headline: Sandpapergate forum announced amid ongoing cricket scandal
summary: A confidential forum for players and staff involved in the 2018 Sandpapergate incident has been set up, offering a safe space to share experiences without a formal investigation. Former coach Darren Lehmann says he has nothing to hide as the cricket community seeks closure.

headline: Cambridge Dictionary names “human” word of the year amid AI debate
summary: The Cambridge Dictionary selected “human” as its 2026 word of the year, emphasizing the distinction between people and machines as artificial intelligence, including ChatGPT, becomes increasingly integrated into daily life.

headline: EU Commission accused of inflating Egypt data to release €2.5bn loan
summary: Leaked documents suggest the European Commission may have softened figures to confirm Egypt met welfare targets, enabling the release of €2.5 billion in loans under a €7.4 billion partnership aimed at stabilising Egypt’s economy and curbing migration.

headline: Study links beer and spirits consumption to higher acute kidney injury risk
summary: Research indicates that drinking beer or spirits raises the likelihood of serious kidney damage, while wine consumption appears protective. Participants consuming nine units of spirits weekly were 26 percent more likely to suffer acute kidney injury than those drinking only one unit.

headline: Australian fund managers eye large stake in Anthropic AI startup
summary: Several Australian fund managers have placed sizable bids for a share of Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI model. While one investor hopes the stake could reach 20% of a portfolio, expectations are tempered.

headline: Analysis of climate policy weighs benefits against adaptation costs
summary: A new report examines the challenges of mitigating climate change, noting that while reducing emissions is crucial, the financial burden of adapting to already-occurring impacts may outweigh the costs of prevention in the near term.

headline: Wall Street expects corporate earnings growth to halve next year
summary: Analysts say global profit growth will drop to 16% next year, down from 33.5%, as the pace of AI-related capital spending slows, reducing earnings momentum for listed companies.

headline: AI pilot audit outperforms accountants but still needs human review
summary: A Big Four firm used AI agents to examine the financial statements of a FTSE 250 company, finding the technology asked better questions than KPMG accountants, though final sign-off still required human intervention.

headline: Rubio rejects claims of systemic US cyber attack after tech outages
summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is zero evidence linking recent disruptions to Microsoft, banks and airlines, dismissing online theories that the United States is under a coordinated cyber assault. He stressed the outages are unrelated incidents.

headline: Raiz Invest promotes CEO Craig Keary to managing director
summary: Fintech platform Raiz Invest announced a board refresh, elevating CEO Craig Keary to managing director as chair Kelly Humphreys steps down, after the firm grew to $2.4 billion in funds under management across 354,000 users.

headline: WA officer feared for colleague before teen was tasered, inquest hears
summary: During an inquest, a Western Australian police officer testified that he feared for a fellow officer’s life before tasering a 16-year-old who was hunting strangers with a knife, before the teen was shot dead.

headline: Thieves steal 1948 Caulfield Cup trophy from racecourse
summary: Melbourne Racing Club reported that the historic 1948 Caulfield Cup trophy, along with bottles of wine and other low-value items, was stolen from Caulfield Racecourse in a break-in.

headline: David Beckham sues over discount-store fragrance sales
summary: Former football star David Beckham has launched a $61 million lawsuit claiming his luxury fragrance line is being sold in petrol stations and discount stores, arguing the placement damages the brand’s image of excellence.

headline: Trump backs return of Huang to Nvidia board
summary: Former US president Donald Trump has voiced support for former Nvidia executive Jensen Huang’s return to the company’s board, citing personal financial interests and broader strategic considerations.

headline: Australia aligns with US on AI policy despite terminology clash
summary: Australia is increasingly coordinating with the United States on artificial-intelligence initiatives, even as the two nations disagree on the terminology used to describe the technology, according to SBS News.

headline: Man admits harbouring fugitive on remote Queensland fishing trip
summary: A court heard that a man accused of sheltering Melbourne fugitive Orijol Rukaj claimed they were on a “boys’ trip” to a remote part of Far North Queensland after the suspect escaped custody at a funeral.

headline: Wage growth continues to lag behind inflation in Australia
summary: Recent figures show wage growth remaining below the rate of inflation, further squeezing household budgets and highlighting ongoing pressures on real incomes across the economy.

headline: Irish fan surprised by pies and crowds at AFL games
summary: Siofra O’Connell, new to Australia from Ireland, described her surprise at the large crowds at women’s AFL matches and the ubiquitous sale of pies, chicken and chips at stadiums.

headline: Putin warns EU of falling behind in industry ahead of US-China talks
summary: President Vladimir Putin told an audience that the European Union is losing its industrial edge and lagging behind competition, framing Russia’s economic resilience ahead of a meeting with US President Trump and Chinese President Xi.

headline: WA council failures described as ‘deeply disappointing’ by minister
summary: Western Australian Minister highlighted that more than two-thirds of the state’s local governments have faced action this year for governance issues and serious misconduct, calling the scale of the problem deeply disappointing.

headline: Safer, slower Targa Tasmania rally draws mixed reactions
summary: The Targa Tasmania tarmac rally returns with reduced speeds and new safety measures after driver deaths, welcomed by some but criticised by others for diminishing competition.

headline: Brisbane Olympic stadium early works cost undisclosed, Gabba demolition bill rises
