headline: Greens propose trust and capital gains tax reforms to secure government support
summary: The Greens offered the government a legislative pathway to pass a minimum tax on trusts and a start-up carve-out in the capital gains tax regime, saying their backing will be crucial for the reforms to pass.

headline: Citi hires Barrenjoey’s Bellofiore to lead new ECM team
summary: Investment bank Citi appointed Bellofiore from Barrenjoey to head its equity capital markets unit, signalling the firm’s growth ambitions as it makes a senior hire at the end of the year.

headline: California files lawsuit against OpenAI over alleged public-nuisance incidents
summary: The state of California sued OpenAI, alleging the AI firm’s actions created a public nuisance and breached laws against unfair or fraudulent business practices, citing incidents that included misuse of Medicare data.

headline: Experts warn stolen Melbourne Cups could be melted down quickly
summary: Security specialists said thieves who stole three Melbourne Cup trophies could soon melt the gold into untraceable forms, making recovery of the iconic sporting awards extremely difficult.

headline: Former Chubb executive alleges fraudulent accounting
summary: Ben Howell, former chief executive of Chubb, says he was dismissed after warning that the insurer’s financial statements were misleading. He claims the company engaged in fraudulent accounting practices, prompting calls for an investigation into its reporting processes.

headline: Artemis and Red Metal start drilling WA Nullarbor copper target
summary: Artemis Resources and partner Red Metal Ltd have begun drilling the Sharon Dam copper-gold anomaly in Western Australia’s Nullarbor region. The 4-kilometre-long target lies deep underground and could represent a major new resource if assay results are positive.

headline: Bunnings to cut 350 technology roles as jobs move offshore
summary: Bunnings announced it will eliminate 350 technology positions, partnering with Tata Consultancy Services to offshore the roles as part of an AI-driven cost-saving strategy. The move adds to a broader trend of job reductions across corporate Australia.

headline: Wallabies under pressure to secure top-three Southern Hemisphere finish
summary: The Australian Wallabies face a crucial test against Wales in the Nations Championship, needing a win to stay on track for a top-three finish among Southern Hemisphere teams. Recent poor form has raised concerns about meeting the season’s target.

headline: Larvotto ships first NSW gold concentrate to Glencore
summary: Larvotto Resources delivered its inaugural gold concentrate from the Hillgrove mine in New South Wales to off-take partner Glencore. The shipment marks the second major production milestone for the junior miner’s development plan.

headline: US Vice-President says decision on 2028 presidential run will come next year
summary: Vice-President Kamala Harris told Fox News she will decide “sometime next year” whether to run for president in 2028, adding she will be fully committed to whichever choice she makes.

headline: EU nations discuss sending asylum seekers to Rwanda
summary: A group of European Union countries are opening talks to begin transferring rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda as early as next year, as part of a coordinated approach to manage migration flows.

headline: One Nation and Greens comment on puberty blocker guidance rejection
summary: Australia’s independent medical council interim advice on puberty blockers was rejected by Queensland and the Northern Territory. Both One Nation and the Greens have weighed in, while LGBTQI+ advocacy groups have welcomed the guidance.

headline: Tasmanian MP declares data-centre developer shares before moratorium bill
summary: A Tasmanian independent MP who tabled a bill for a moratorium on new data centres disclosed holdings in a property giant whose pipeline is almost 80 percent data-centre projects, raising questions about a potential conflict of interest.

headline: Oversized wind-farm convoy strains Australia’s transport network
summary: A convoy of oversized trucks carrying 100-metre-long wind-farm components required 30,000 police escorts and a 278 km detour, highlighting the fragility of Australia’s road and port infrastructure in supporting large renewable-energy projects.

headline: Dolores Huerta honoured at California state capitol ceremony
summary: Labor leader Dolores Huerta was commemorated at a ceremony in Sacramento, where officials praised her role in co-founding the United Farm Workers and her lifelong advocacy for civil-rights and feminist causes.

headline: Alaska Senate race remains tight as votes are still being counted
summary: The contest between Democrat Mary Peltola and incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan in Alaska’s Senate race is still unresolved, with counting ongoing and Peltola currently leading.

headline: Aureka reports shallow gold discovery at Victoria’s Irvine project
summary: Aureka Ltd announced the identification of shallow, visible gold at its Irvine project in Victoria, boosting expectations of expanding its 398,300-ounce inferred resource towards a potential million-ounce deposit.

headline: Backpacker visa cap raised after industry backlash
summary: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has increased the third-year working holiday visa cap by 20,000 places following criticism from agriculture, tourism and hospitality groups. The change comes after a delayed rollout of a new visa ballot system, which remains postponed until next year and will still exempt British applicants.

headline: Rio Tinto to pay $250 million for Panguna mine remediation
summary: Rio Tinto has agreed to a $250 million settlement to begin cleaning up the abandoned Panguna mine in Papua New Guinea, addressing longstanding environmental damage and community grievances stemming from the mine’s closure in 1989.

headline: Former Pakistani PM Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care
summary: Imran Khan, Pakistan’s ex-prime minister who has been incarcerated since August 2023, says he is urgently seeking medical treatment, fearing his health may not survive without it.

headline: Hippo Fiona receives care after swallowing a knit hat
summary: Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo’s celebrity hippo, is under veterinary observation after ingesting a knit hat that fell into her enclosure, with staff working to ensure the hat passes safely.

headline: Locksley launches high-grade copper-gold drill programme in NSW
summary: Locksley Resources has begun a diamond-drilling campaign at the Iron Duke project in New South Wales, targeting high-grade copper-gold extensions as part of a broader 26,000-metre district-wide exploration effort.

headline: David Jones suppliers protest over $180m debt
summary: Suppliers to Australian retailer David Jones say the chain owes at least $180 million, alongside over $200 million to lenders and more than $10 million to staff, sparking anger and calls for urgent payment solutions.

headline: Fed chair warns AI impact on jobs and rates
summary: Federal Reserve chairman Kevin Warsh says artificial intelligence is at a turning point and could reshape employment and influence future interest-rate policy, prompting the central bank to consider how AI will affect the economy.

headline: Father sues state over two-week hotel quarantine after child’s death
summary: Hayden Flinn has filed a lawsuit against the state, claiming the refusal of a compassionate exemption forced his family to remain in hotel quarantine for two weeks, during which his child died.

headline: BBC launches Hausa programme for out-of-school Nigerian children
summary: The BBC World Service has introduced a new Hausa-language programme aimed at reaching millions of Nigerian children who are unable to attend school due to poverty, child marriage and kidnapping.

headline: Royal commission into Big Build hears bikie gang figure as probe continues
summary: The second week of the Big Build royal commission saw former bikie gang member Joel Leavitt appear before the inquiry as investigations into the infrastructure project’s management persist.

headline: ASX drops as miners slump and Mayne Pharma receives $604m takeover offer
summary: The Australian sharemarket fell in early trade, led by losses in mining and energy stocks and a pull-back in Nvidia-related shares. At the same time Mayne Pharma announced a $604 million bid from a Hungarian drug group, lifting its share price sharply.

headline: United Airlines resolves system outage affecting departing flights
summary: United Airlines confirmed that a technical outage was fixed, with no impact on flights already in the air and no evidence of a cyber-attack.

headline: Software bug triggers outages at major US banks and money-transfer service
summary: Customers of two large US banks and a popular money-transfer platform reported access problems after a software error caused widespread service disruptions.

headline: AFL announces five rule tweaks ahead of 2027 season
summary: The Australian Football League released five changes to its rules, including new powers for the Match Review Officer, as it prepares for the 2027 competition.

headline: William and Kate travel Mumbai metro during three-day India visit
summary: The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge rode the Mumbai metro as part of a three-day trip that includes a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

headline: Scammers use fake sites and listings to target travellers
summary: Travelers are being duped by fraudulent websites and listings that impersonate airlines, hotels and other services. The scams are becoming increasingly convincing, prompting warnings about the tactics used to lure victims.

headline: WA teachers’ union rejects proposed pay offer
summary: The Western Australian teachers’ union has turned down the latest wage proposal, calling it inadequate. Negotiations are set to continue as the union seeks a better deal for its members.

headline: Druckenmiller family office sells AMD, Sandisk, buys SpaceX and Palantir
summary: The family office of investor Stanley Druckenmiller reduced its holdings in chip makers AMD and Sandisk during the third quarter, while increasing positions in SpaceX and Palantir.

headline: Indian AI start-ups address road and land record challenges
summary: Dozens of Indian artificial-intelligence start-ups are deploying solutions to fix the country’s broken road infrastructure and chaotic land-record systems, expanding into sectors such as legal-tech and healthcare.

headline: Nvidia leadership change raises AI market concerns
summary: Nvidia’s ousted chief executive faces scrutiny over how its most advanced chips reached China, despite backing from Donald Trump and Elon Musk. Analyst Jim Cramer argues the shake-up will not derail the broader AI boom, but investors remain wary of supply-chain and geopolitical risks.

headline: Russia seeks joint statement after US-China-Russia summit
summary: Following the unprecedented meeting of leaders from the United States, China and Russia, Moscow is pushing for a joint communiqué to summarise the outcomes of the trilateral summit.

headline: First native olive-ridley turtles released off California coast
summary: Seventy-five hatchlings from the historic olive-ridley nests discovered on California’s west coast have been released into the Pacific, marking the state’s first native sea-turtle population.

headline: Police raid home after Melbourne Cup trophies stolen
summary: Three trophies belonging to champion horse Makybe Diva were taken from Flemington racecourse. A raid on a Mount Waverley residence failed to recover the stolen items.

headline: Coroner releases cause of death for Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner
summary: Louisiana officials determined that Kenan “Ken” Urker died from accidental polysubstance drug toxicity, concluding the investigation into his death.

headline: Convicts sit Korea's toughest university entrance exam
summary: Eleven inmates at the Mandela Boys’ School will sit South Korea’s notoriously difficult Suneung university entrance exam alongside thousands of other young candidates.

headline: China showcases AI hub while masking underlying challenges
summary: China is hosting global leaders in its AI-focused cityscape, but observers note that beneath the high-tech façade lie significant economic and regulatory hurdles.

headline: Aschenbrenner fund bought AI stocks before market rout
summary: Leopold Aschenbrenner’s hedge fund, which nearly collapsed over the summer, added positions in artificial-intelligence shares just before the sector’s sharp decline in October, according to the report.

headline: Study finds many Amazon Black Friday deals offer no savings
summary: Analysis of Amazon’s Black Friday promotions over the past two years shows that almost one-third of the advertised deals provided no discount at all, prompting the retailer to push back against the findings.

headline: Gilbert + Tobin private-equity partner resigns
summary: Josselsohn, a partner in Gilbert + Tobin’s corporate advisory group and a recognised figure in Australia’s private-equity community, has stepped down from his role at the firm.

headline: Victorian Premier Ben Carroll grilled over poor Labor polling
summary: During a live press event ahead of early voting, Premier Ben Carroll faced tough questions about the Labor Party’s slipping poll numbers as the state election campaign intensifies.

headline: Mayor calls for inquiry into western Victoria mining licences
summary: The mayor of Horsham Rural City Council is urging an investigation into the approval process for mining licences across western Victoria, citing concerns over the current mineral sands planning scheme.

headline: Big-wave surfers tackle Mavericks during Super El-Niño swells
summary: Professional surfers converged on California’s Mavericks Beach to ride massive, storm-driven waves generated by the current Super El-Niño, an event dubbed “Monster Day” by participants.

headline: Berkshire Hathaway adds Delta stake, trims Bank of America holding
summary: In the third quarter, Berkshire Hathaway increased its investment in airline Delta while reducing its position in Bank of America, part of a broader reshuffle of its equity portfolio.

headline: Chinese fashion platform Xiaohongshu boosts local brands as Nike, Lululemon falter
summary: A report notes that while Nike and Lululemon face slowing sales in China, the social-commerce app Xiaohongshu is helping domestic fashion labels gain traction among Chinese consumers.

headline: Australian actor becomes new face of The Hunger Games franchise
summary: An Australian performer has been announced as the latest lead representing The Hunger Games series, joining a two-decade-long franchise that centres on resistance against oppression.

headline: Chris Bowen unveils ambitious climate plan at COP31
summary: Australia’s climate minister, Chris Bowen, presented a draft agreement at COP31 calling for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, an earlier net-zero target and increased funding for climate adaptation.

headline: Prince William and Princess Catherine ride Mumbai metro
summary: During a visit to India, Prince William and Princess Catherine travelled on Mumbai’s metro system, joining cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar for a street-level game before the ride.

headline: U.S. dollar’s AI-driven surge could threaten stock markets
summary: Analysts warn that the U.S. dollar’s recent climb to its strongest level in 18 months, driven by artificial-intelligence trading, may act as a “wrecking ball” for equity markets.

headline: Treasurer Jim Chalmers promises modest mid-year spending cuts
summary: In the upcoming December budget update, Treasurer Jim Chalmers confirmed a “substantial” but not excessive package of savings will be introduced to the Australian government’s mid-year financial plan.

headline: Jannik Sinner prefers low-key, crowd-free holidays
summary: Top tennis player Jannik Sinner says his ideal vacation involves no plans and no crowds, offering a glimpse into how the ATP Tour’s relentless schedule influences his downtime.

headline: Trump’s accounts trade up to $97.5 million in Nvidia after brief
summary: Following a briefing on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged ties to a Chinese spy, former President Donald Trump’s investment accounts bought up to $1 million of Nvidia shares, totaling roughly $97.5 million in trades.

headline: Autonomous CRM systems automate sales and service tasks
summary: New autonomous CRM platforms can handle functions across departments, from generating sales quotes to answering routine service enquiries, reducing manual workload and speeding up customer interactions for businesses.

headline: Berkshire doubles stake in US home-builder Lennar
summary: Berkshire Hathaway increased its investment in the US housing market last quarter, nearly doubling its holding in home builder Lennar as part of a broader push into residential construction.

headline: Report urges UK Labour to fund ‘new deal’ for youth jobs
summary: A Labour-commissioned report calls for billions of pounds of spending on welfare, education, health and guaranteed job support to tackle a surge in NEETs approaching one million young people in Britain.

headline: Electric vehicles enter motorsport but fans remain skeptical
summary: Motorsport organisers are introducing electric vehicles to race tracks, yet many traditional fans remain unconvinced, preferring the sound and smell of petrol engines.

headline: BOM investigates possible tornado after NSW storm
summary: The Bureau of Meteorology is assessing radar data and reports following a severe storm that hit the NSW coast, confirming the possibility of a tornado near South West Rocks.

headline: Personal AI agents set to appear in Australian businesses
summary: During the holiday season, many Australian companies will encounter personal AI agents for the first time, prompting advice to engage rather than block these emerging tools.

headline: Police continue hunt for drive-by shooters after teen death
summary: Queensland police have released CCTV footage as the investigation into a drive-by shooting that killed a 19-year-old in Jimboomba continues, with no arrests yet made.

headline: Short-term rentals driven by non-holiday travel
summary: Research shows that 30-40 % of demand for short-term rental stays comes from travellers on business or other non-holiday trips, challenging the perception that most bookings are leisure-focused.

headline: Software bug disrupts JPMorgan consumer banking services
summary: A temporary software glitch is affecting JPMorgan Chase’s consumer banking platforms, with no evidence of malicious actors or a wider impact on other banks.

headline: Domestic-violence survivor struggles to find emergency housing
summary: A mother fleeing domestic violence faced an immediate crisis in securing safe accommodation for herself and her children after leaving the abusive home.

headline: AI paradox: abundant expertise, scarce judgment
summary: An analysis notes that while knowledge and AI tools are increasingly accessible, the ability to interpret data and apply sound judgement remains limited, creating a paradox for businesses and policymakers.

headline: Sharon AI says debt markets still open for AI compute funding
summary: Sharon AI co-founder and CEO James Manning says the digital infrastructure firm can still raise money in debt markets to fund AI compute capacity, positioning itself apart from rivals in the global AI race.

headline: Hundreds of Australians feel tremors from Indonesian 6.6 quake
summary: More than 460 Australians reported feeling the shaking from a magnitude-6.6 earthquake that struck Indonesia, with reports of rattling windows and furniture across several states.

headline: Western Australian miners compete for skilled migrants amid AUKUS jobs crunch
summary: WA mining companies are intensifying recruitment of skilled migrants as the AUKUS defence programme drives a shortage of qualified workers on the west coast.

headline: Putin, Trump and Xi meet in China, analysts call summit farcical
summary: Leaders of Russia, the United States and China gathered in China for a summit billed as a modern-day Yalta, but commentators argue the meeting is unlikely to produce any meaningful division of global influence.

headline: Tim Wilson argues big business is engine of Australian economy
summary: Former minister Tim Wilson contends that engaging with large corporations, rather than confronting them, is essential for Australia to achieve its full economic potential.

headline: OpenAI appoints four independent evaluators to strengthen safety work
summary: OpenAI has signed agreements with four external evaluators to enhance its AI safety and security programmes following a series of high-profile incidents.

headline: Cricketer Usman Khawaja avoids sandpaper questions on TV
summary: Usman Khawaja made his first television appearance since the 7.30 interview, steering clear of queries about the sandpaper controversy that led to his suspension.

headline: WA driver avoids jail after crashing into fuel bowser
summary: A Western Australian man who collided with a fuel bowser, claiming he thought the world was ending, has escaped an immediate prison sentence.

headline: Russell Brand investigated over prison message to victims
summary: The convicted rapist faces a prison investigation after allegedly breaching rules by posting an ‘appalling’ message proclaiming his innocence.

headline: Houthi advance in Yemen could destabilise global economy
summary: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels are making territorial gains in Yemen, raising concerns about wider economic repercussions worldwide.

headline: Victorian schools devastated after VCE language subjects withdrawn
summary: Community language schools in Victoria are shocked after the education department ended VCE registration for language subjects, leaving many students without a pathway to certification.

headline: Eli Lilly’s new weight-loss pill approved for Australian market
summary: The Australian regulator has approved Eli Lilly’s daily weight-loss tablet orforglipron, with shipments expected to arrive in the coming days.

headline: Nvidia’s AI chip boom continues despite founder’s departure
summary: Even after Jensen Huang stepped down, demand for AI chips remains strong, with customers shifting who pays for the technology as the market sustains its growth.

headline: Coalition proposes rule change to aid multigenerational homes
summary: The opposition government in Victoria wants to amend building regulations so that houses with an additional kitchen are still classified as a single dwelling, making it easier for families to live together across generations. The proposal aims to increase housing flexibility without creating new separate properties.

headline: Kalshi signals move into stock trading
summary: Financial platform Kalshi announced plans to add stock trading to its product suite, marking a shift from its current focus on event-based contracts toward traditional equity markets. The move reflects the company’s strategy to broaden its user base and compete more directly with established brokerage services.

headline: Chevron close to $5bn acquisition of Blackstone-backed oil producer
summary: Chevron is nearing a deal worth about five billion dollars to buy Beacon Offshore Energy, a Gulf of Mexico oil producer backed by Blackstone. The transaction would expand Chevron’s deep-water portfolio and position the company ahead of rival bidders seeking to increase offshore production capacity.

headline: Coronial inquest says Perth teen was self-radicalised before police shooting
summary: The inquest into the death of 16-year-old James Hollands, who was shot by police at a Bunnings store in Perth, heard he acted alone and was self-radicalised, harbouring a desire to kill local males. The findings raise questions about youth radicalisation and police response.

headline: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East amid Iran tensions
summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt, the United States’ third carrier deployed to the region, has entered the Middle East, bringing thousands of additional troops. The move comes as President Trump alternates between threatening further strikes on Iran and claiming the eight-month war is effectively over, heightening regional uncertainty.

headline: 14-year-old Leihani Zoric wins World Games surfing title
summary: Byron Bay’s Leihani Zoric made history by becoming the youngest woman to claim the World Games surfing championship at just 14 years old. Her victory stunned the competition and highlighted the rising talent emerging from Australia’s coastal surf community.

headline: Pope Francis struck by rosary in Peru farewell Mass
summary: During a farewell Mass in Peru, Pope Francis was hit in the face by what appeared to be a rosary, prompting a brief pause in the ceremony.

headline: Albanese raises Laos methanol poisoning deaths with prime minister
summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese discussed the recent deaths of two Australian backpackers from methanol poisoning with the Laotian prime minister, who pledged a review of related criminal trials and any new evidence. The diplomatic engagement underscores concerns over safety for Australians travelling abroad.

headline: Albanese signs US-led AI supply-chain pact at Quad summit
summary: At the Quad leaders’ summit in Manila, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese joined the United States and Japan in a pact to safeguard artificial-intelligence supply chains and critical infrastructure. The agreement aims to counter China’s growing influence over AI technologies while strengthening cooperation among the four nations.

headline: Victorian teacher under investigation moves to Northern Territory
summary: A teacher from Victoria, accused of extensive grooming communications involving nearly 100 messages and private meetings, relocated to the Northern Territory to continue working while the investigation proceeds. Authorities are examining the allegations amid concerns about safeguarding in schools.

headline: Wales’ record tackles fuel All Blacks win, Wallabies await clash
summary: In a recent test match, Wales set a new benchmark for tackles, exhausting themselves against the All Blacks, who secured victory. The Wallabies now look ahead to their upcoming encounter, hoping to avoid a similar fatigue-induced performance.

headline: California sues OpenAI over alleged security breach
summary: Attorney General Rob Bonta claims OpenAI misled the public and endangered safety after a vulnerability involving the Hugging Face platform was exposed.

headline: Online bookmaker fined for inducement scheme targeting netball club
summary: An online betting operator was penalised after a sustained, employee-facilitated inducement scheme was uncovered involving a community netball club’s social media. The fine follows investigations that revealed the bookmaker had offered incentives to club members, breaching gambling regulations.

headline: Brisbane luxury apartment owners sue council over noisy neighbour air-con
summary: Owners of high-end apartments in Brisbane’s Fish Lane have taken the city council to the Queensland Ombudsman, alleging that an excessively loud air-conditioning unit in a neighbouring unit is causing a persistent disturbance. The dispute raises questions about noise regulations in multi-unit developments.

headline: Forensic expert says Epstein autopsy suggests homicide
summary: Professor Michael Freeman, a forensic specialist, told BBC Newsnight that his analysis of autopsy photographs indicates the injuries on convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein are consistent with a homicide rather than suicide. The comments add a new dimension to ongoing debates about the circumstances of his death.

headline: David Jones holds first creditors meeting as administrator seeks buyer
summary: David Jones convened its inaugural creditors' meeting as administrators assess options. Lender Hilco injected additional funds to purchase stock, aiming to keep the retailer trading while a new owner is sought. Shares opened lower amid broader market declines.

headline: Technology lowers barriers for Australian entrepreneurs
summary: New digital tools are making it easier for Australian start-ups to launch and scale, reducing costs and simplifying access to markets and capital.

headline: Sydney private school suspends students over antisemitic post
summary: Students at a private school in western Sydney were suspended after the principal said an online act deemed antisemitic violated respect for human dignity. The school is investigating the incident.

headline: Eli Lilly announces new deal beyond obesity; Nvidia warning issued
summary: Eli Lilly disclosed a new commercial agreement unrelated to its obesity drug, while analysts issued a cautionary note on Nvidia's recent market moves. The updates came in a daily market commentary aimed at traders.

headline: UK plans strip asylum seekers of grace period, allow immediate removal
summary: The Home Office will remove the five-day grace period for asylum seekers whose appeals have been exhausted, permitting immediate detention and removal. Refugee charities warned the change would cause unnecessary distress and anxiety.

headline: Survey finds half of senior Queensland doctors worry fatigue may cause errors
summary: A new survey of senior doctors in Queensland shows 50% are concerned that fatigue could lead to clinical mistakes, and 23% say they may quit within two years because of burnout.

headline: UK to extend Palantir NHS data platform contract until 2029
summary: The Department of Health and Social Care will prolong Palantir’s federated data platform contract for two more years, delaying a planned break clause until 2029 to allow time for British firms to take over the service.

headline: Australia backs down on tougher backpacker visa work requirements
summary: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said the government will negotiate on the proposed increase in regional work days for backpackers, after industry pressure led to a reversal of the planned rise from 88 to 120 days.

headline: Massachusetts judge sets retrial date for Lindsay Clancy
summary: A judge in Massachusetts has scheduled a retrial for Lindsay Clancy for late March, with lawyers to discuss trial logistics and media arrangements later this year.

headline: Medical Board imposes conditions on surgeon over patient death
summary: The Medical Board of Australia placed conditions on surgeon Stefaan De Clercq after a patient died at Bundaberg Hospital in October 2023, following a board investigation.

headline: Socceroos coach Popovic says future uncertain after Asian Cup postponement
summary: Tony Popovic admitted his contract talks with Football Australia are pending and his future as Socceroos coach remains unclear after the Asian Cup was postponed.

headline: Tasmania faces long colonoscopy waitlist
summary: Nearly 4,000 Tasmanians are waiting for urgent endoscopy procedures, highlighting systemic delays in the public health system. Critics describe the backlog as part of a complex, under-resourced framework that needs reform to reduce waiting times for vital diagnostics.

headline: Robert Pattinson announced as next James Bond
summary: Actor Robert Pattinson, known for recent roles in major films including Christopher Nolan’s latest project, has been confirmed as the next actor to portray the iconic British spy James Bond. The casting adds further anticipation to the upcoming Bond franchise installment.

headline: Brexit veterans launch rival anti-EU campaigns
summary: Former Leave.EU and Vote Leave figures have started separate groups – Enough Official and Stay Out – to defend Brexit, claiming a cooperative approach despite past animosity between the campaigns.

headline: Man arrested but $3 million Makybe Diva trophies still missing
summary: Police have detained a suspect in the theft of three Makybe Diva Melbourne Cup trophies, but the $3 million prizes have yet to be recovered.

headline: Labour seeks solutions to youth unemployment crisis
summary: Former cabinet minister Alan Milburn, leading a government review, urges Labour MPs to address the near-million young Australians out of work and education, warning of a ‘downward escalator’ into long-term benefit dependence.

headline: Anthropic IPO draws trader interest in derivatives market
summary: Traders are focusing on the upcoming Anthropic IPO, with bullish signals emerging in the derivatives space as investors anticipate the AI firm’s market debut.

headline: Saudi-backed forces face criticism over Yemen strategy
summary: Anti-Houthi groups accuse Saudi-aligned troops of missteps after a pull-back from key positions in Yemen, while Riyadh says the redeployment aims to break the siege of Taiz and protect Aden.

headline: Analysts say Nvidia focus may mask Disney earnings opportunity
summary: Market commentary suggests that intense attention on Nvidia could be causing investors to overlook potential upside in Disney’s upcoming earnings report.

headline: Quad unity tested by US-India tensions in Manila
summary: The Quad’s cohesion faces strain as diplomatic frictions between the United States and India affect relationships with the Philippines, raising questions about the alliance’s future direction.

headline: Australia cracks down on illicit tobacco trade
summary: The government has intensified enforcement against black-market tobacco products, aiming to curb illegal sales while assessing whether additional measures are needed to address persistent addiction issues.

headline: Tasmania seeks partners to fund Hobart stadium cost overruns
summary: Facing a budget shortfall on its $1.13 billion stadium project, the Tasmanian government is looking for financial partners to help cover escalating expenses and keep the development on track.

headline: US moves to curb AI chip smuggling amid push to reinstate Nvidia CEO
summary: US authorities are stepping up actions to stop the smuggling of AI chips, coinciding with political pressure to reinstate former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang after his recent resignation.

headline: Anthropic’s governance model scrutinised amid AI power concentration concerns
summary: Analysts question whether Anthropic’s unique governance structure adequately checks the extraordinary power of its Claude AI system, highlighting broader issues of boardroom control in big-tech firms.

headline: Report urges lower National Insurance for under-25s to boost jobs
summary: Former minister Alan Milburn’s upcoming report recommends gradually reducing employer National Insurance contributions for workers under 25, arguing the move would help create more jobs in the UK.

headline: Analysis says Rudd's abandoned mining tax would have added $135 billion to budget
summary: A Parliamentary Budget Office analysis finds that the mining tax dismissed by former Prime Minister Kevin Rudd in 2010 could have delivered about $135 billion in budget surpluses, highlighting the fiscal impact of the abandoned policy.

headline: Doctors warn antibiotic resistance could cause millions of Australian deaths
summary: Australia’s peak medical body cautions that rising antibiotic resistance threatens modern medicine and could lead to millions of deaths if not addressed, urging urgent action to preserve treatment effectiveness.

headline: Westpac to cut nearly 300 jobs as bank trims workforce
summary: Westpac, Australia’s oldest bank, is rolling out job cuts affecting close to 300 positions, adding to a series of staff reductions across the sector despite no headline-grabbing announcement.

headline: Companies channel Trump tariff refunds into executive bonuses
summary: ProPublica finds at least nine firms that received refunds for tariffs imposed under Donald Trump have redirected the money to corporate leadership bonuses rather than passing savings to consumers.

headline: EU sanctions target Russia’s richest woman, Wildberries founder
summary: The European Union has imposed sanctions on the founder of Wildberries, Russia’s largest online retailer, as part of its latest measures against individuals linked to the war in Ukraine.

headline: COP31 draft aims to draw out parties ahead of final decision
summary: Australia’s COP31 president says the first draft of a potential cover decision, released with several days of negotiation remaining, is intended to highlight areas of agreement and disagreement among parties.

headline: Five EU states propose Rwanda ‘return hubs’ for illegal migrants
summary: Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece announced plans to establish offshore centres in Rwanda for migrants without legal status, a scheme expected to face legal challenges and criticised as a moral failing.

headline: U.S. crude oil price falls to $87 a barrel
summary: Crude oil prices slipped to $87 a barrel as analysts project a fourth-quarter surplus in global supply, driven by recovering exports from the Middle East.

headline: Five EU states back Rwanda migrant deportation hub
summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands announced a joint “return hub” in Rwanda for asylum seekers whose applications have been rejected, aiming to curb irregular migration.

headline: US hyperscaler datacenters emit as much CO₂ as Denmark
summary: Research shows the rapid build-out of large AI-focused datacenters in the United States generated about 25.7 million tonnes of carbon dioxide, roughly matching Denmark’s annual emissions.

headline: SpaceX Starship launch succeeds amid tech sell-off
summary: SpaceX achieved a mostly successful Starship launch, reinforcing its lead in the space race even as a broader technology market downturn weighed on its share price.

headline: Prediction market odds rise for Tesla-SpaceX merger
summary: Odds that Tesla and SpaceX will merge by April 2027 climbed to 62% from 27% after speculation intensified about a possible integration of the two Elon Musk-led companies.

headline: US Justice Department warns Warren over future investigations
summary: The Justice Department sent a letter to the likely Senate Banking Committee chair, cautioning Democrats about plans for new investigations following their recent electoral gains.

headline: Analysts flag 13 S&P 500 stocks could jump 70% next year
summary: Consensus earnings estimates have risen for a group of S&P 500 companies, especially semiconductor makers, leading analysts to project potential gains of up to 70% over the coming year.

headline: US homeowners launch property-tax revolt over rising costs
summary: A growing movement of American homeowners is pushing for cuts to property taxes as they grapple with escalating housing expenses, seeking relief through legislative action.

headline: Robert Pattinson announced as new James Bond
summary: British actor Robert Pattinson has been confirmed as the next James Bond, taking over the role after Daniel Craig’s departure.

headline: Trump backs Jensen Huang return as Nvidia CEO amid scandal
summary: Former President Donald Trump said he would welcome Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief, dismissing the company’s scandal as not a national-security risk, while the Commerce Department moves to close a data-center export loophole.

headline: Grammy nominations feature Tame Impala and Raye among women-dominated list
summary: The 2027 Grammy nominations were announced with a strong female presence, led by Raye and Rosalía. Australian act Tame Impala secured a spot among the few male nominees, while legends like Dolly Parton received posthumous nods.

headline: US colleges face financial strain as international enrolments plunge
summary: Higher tuition costs and tighter immigration rules have caused a sharp drop in international student numbers at US universities, threatening the financial stability of many campuses that rely on overseas tuition revenue.

headline: Queensland businessmen plead guilty to selling Russian jet engines to China
summary: Two businessmen from Queensland were convicted of attempting to export Russian fighter-jet engines to China, breaching export controls. Their case was highlighted alongside former US President Trump’s comments on Putin’s stance in the Ukraine conflict.

headline: Prince William and Kate begin India visit with street cricket
summary: The Prince and Princess of Wales start their India trip in Mumbai, playing street cricket before attending the Earthshot Prize ceremony, marking a high-profile royal visit to the region.

headline: FDA rejects Summit Therapeutics’ lung-cancer drug pending survival data
summary: The US Food and Drug Administration declined to approve Summit Therapeutics’ lung-cancer candidate, stating the drug must demonstrate an overall survival benefit before it can be cleared for use.

headline: Jefferies fund relaxes lending checks for iron-ore traders amid fraud accusations
summary: Jefferies-backed fund Point Bonita eased verification requirements for iron-ore traders, allowing Glencore to bypass invoice checks from Radiant World and Sapphire despite ongoing fraud allegations.

headline: Two men charged after van runs over man in Birmingham flags incident
summary: Police charged two suspects in connection with a May incident in Birmingham where a man was struck by a van after flags were removed from a lamp-post, leaving him with leg injuries.

headline: Novo’s Wegovy trial shows weight loss in six-year-olds
summary: A Novo Nordisk trial found that the Wegovy injection helped nearly 80% of children as young as six lose more than 10% of their BMI, marking the first data on the drug’s effect in under-12s.

headline: NYC mayor disbands controversial police strategic response group
summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the dissolution of the Strategic Response Group, a police unit criticized for aggressive tactics against protesters, and introduced a new community-safety division.

headline: Warren Buffett donates $5.5 billion in charitable giving
summary: Berkshire Hathaway chairman emeritus Warren Buffett announced a $5.5 billion donation in his Thanksgiving letter, saying kindness compounds. He still holds 182,140 Class A shares, valued at roughly $162 billion.

headline: Bitcoin falls below $62,000 after liquidation cascade
summary: Bitcoin slipped under $62,000 as a wave of long-position liquidations hit the market, pushing the cryptocurrency below key technical support levels before a modest rebound.

headline: Estonia shuts Russia border crossings after alleged drone factory arson
summary: The Estonian government ordered the closure of all Russia border crossings, blaming a recent attempted arson at a drone factory on Russian actors, a claim the Kremlin denies.

headline: NSW bill to boost Mount Pleasant coal output raises corruption concerns
summary: A New South Wales bill that would allow MACH Energy to increase production at the Mount Pleasant coal mine is being criticised for giving the resources minister sweeping powers that could create a serious corruption risk.

headline: Home insurance premiums in Australia up nearly 50% in five years
summary: Australian homeowners face premiums that have risen almost 50% over the past five years, with some policies costing up to $8,000 a year, forcing many to choose between coverage and unaffordability.

headline: New photos reveal life in 1946 Pilbara strike camps
summary: A collection of photographs uncovered beneath a wardrobe provides a rare glimpse of daily life in the Aboriginal workers' strike camps of Pilbara in 1946, eight decades after the protest.

headline: UK warns mushroom grow kits may spread invasive species
summary: British horticultural experts have advised against using popular golden oyster mushroom grow kits, classifying them as high-risk invasive species that could damage native woodlands.

headline: Major NFT marketplace announces closure after five-year boom
summary: A leading non-fungible token marketplace is shutting down, marking the end of a five-year cycle that saw rapid growth followed by a bust, and highlighting the risks of speculative digital-asset investments.

headline: Brisbane attracts more visitors while resident satisfaction falls
summary: Tourism and cultural events are drawing increasing numbers of visitors to inner-city Brisbane, but local residents report declining satisfaction due to concerns over housing affordability and safety.

headline: Ineos settles dispute with Ben Ainslie over America’s Cup yacht
summary: Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos Group has reached an out-of-court settlement with Sir Ben Ainslie, ending a legal fight over the £180 million yacht built for the 2024 America’s Cup. The agreement resolves claims that Ineos refused to return the vessel, avoiding a trial scheduled for next year.

headline: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress faces earnings test after Jensen Huang exit
summary: Less than a week after Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure, Nvidia’s interim chief Colette Kress leads the company into its first earnings report, confronting key questions about performance and strategy.

headline: Andy Burnham launches fund to restore UK lidos
summary: UK Labour leader Andy Burnham announced a public fund to refurbish threatened outdoor swimming pools, known as lidos. The initiative follows a surge in demand for open-air swimming and aims to preserve historic art-deco facilities built in the 1930s.

headline: Israeli opposition leader calls for probe into PM’s office
summary: Gadi Eisenkot, the main challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, has demanded an investigation into the Prime Minister’s Office after allegations that it fabricated claims of electoral fraud. The request adds pressure ahead of upcoming elections.

headline: David Beckham’s brand sues over unauthorised fragrance sales
summary: DB Ventures, the company owned by former footballer David Beckham, has filed a lawsuit against a distributor after its fragrance range was found for sale in Poundland and a petrol-station bargain bin, which the brand says were not authorised retail channels.

headline: American basketball player arrested with 75 lb of marijuana in Nigeria
summary: U.S. basketball player Greene Da’monte Khiree was detained at Lagos airport after customs officials discovered approximately 33.9 kg of marijuana in his luggage. Nigerian authorities said the alleged smuggling offence carries a life-sentence.

headline: Ukraine strikes Kerch bridge linking Crimea to Russia
summary: Ukrainian forces hit the Kerch bridge with a kamikaze drone, damaging an arch and temporarily halting road traffic. The attack, part of a broader drone barrage, left thousands of drivers stranded and underscored the bridge’s strategic importance.

headline: Exiled Guatemalan Nobel laureate’s ashes returned home
summary: The ashes of Miguel Ángel Asturias, a Guatemalan poet, writer and diplomat who died in exile in 1974, have been repatriated to Guatemala, allowing a symbolic homecoming for the Nobel-prize-winning author.

headline: Man sentenced for attempted murder of three children
summary: Riad Bouchaker received a prison term after being convicted of the attempted murder of three children in November 2023. The court handed down the sentence following a trial that highlighted the severity of the offence.

headline: Analysis: Putin, Trump and Xi cannot form a new ‘big three’
summary: A Financial Times commentary argues that the leaders of the United States, China and Russia are unable to dominate global affairs as a unified bloc, citing structural, strategic and domestic constraints that prevent them from carving up the world together.

headline: Nvidia shares fall after US restricts chip access to China
summary: Nvidia’s stock continued to decline after the US Commerce Department announced a rule limiting China’s remote access to advanced chips. The move follows harsh comments from the US government about the chipmaker’s ties to China, adding pressure on the company’s share price.

headline: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal after sexual assault conviction
summary: French actor Gérard Depardieu has withdrawn his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a Paris film set. In a written statement he accepted the verdict and apologised to the victims, confirming the court’s original ruling.

headline: Pakistan floods linked to intensified monsoon rainfall
summary: University lecturer Imran Lodhi describes how climate-driven intense monsoon rains caused devastating floods in Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan, displacing families and prompting urgent relief efforts.

headline: Rising shipping costs could limit holiday inventory
summary: Transport executives say higher freight rates are prompting retailers to curb stock of big-ticket holiday items, making some products harder to find for shoppers.

headline: UK’s oldest renewable projects set for £9bn subsidy windfall
summary: Analysis shows that legacy wind and solar farms in Britain could receive nearly £9 billion in payments next year as market prices surge, prompting calls to reform the subsidy scheme.

headline: Eurovision Asia footage edited in Malaysia over LGBTQ content
summary: The European Broadcasting Union says it will write to the Asian contest licence holder after Malaysia’s TV3 cut drag and gay jury footage from the first Eurovision Asia broadcast.

headline: Teen AFL hopeful Lucas Robinson eyes legend’s footsteps ahead of draft
summary: Prospective draftee Lucas Robinson reveals the Australian Football League great he wants to emulate as he prepares for this week’s national draft.

headline: Xi, Trump and Putin to meet in Shenzhen for trilateral talks
summary: China, the United States and Russia will hold a first-of-its-kind trilateral meeting in Shenzhen during the APEC summit, with leaders Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin expected to discuss world-peace topics such as denuclearisation.

headline: Israeli military uploads 3.5 million photos to Amazon cloud for facial-recognition analysis
summary: Leaked documents reveal Israel moved millions of images of Palestinians to Amazon’s cloud platform to use its facial-recognition tools during the Gaza conflict.

headline: Investor warns fame can undermine tech founders at Nvidia and Tesla
summary: A prominent shareholder argues that the celebrity status of CEOs at Nvidia and Tesla can negatively affect both personal lives and company performance.

headline: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
summary: Separate attacks in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng have killed 17 people, highlighting the country’s ongoing struggle with violent crime.

headline: Robert Irwin and sprinter Gout among Queensland’s Australian of the Year nominees
summary: Conservationist Robert Irwin and 2024 sprint champion Gout Gout join two other Queensland advocates as finalists for the state’s Australian of the Year awards.

headline: Two passengers trapped atop Perth ferris wheel after operator leaves early
summary: WorkSafe will investigate after a Perth ferris wheel operator departed before the ride finished, leaving two paying riders stranded at the top.

headline: NSW inquest hears birth keeper told mother of deceased baby to ‘go home and rest’
summary: Coroner’s court hears that a birth keeper advised a pregnant woman, whose baby later died, to return home despite urgent medical advice to seek emergency care.

headline: Four-year-old injured after car crashes into Perth daycare fence
summary: A vehicle struck the fence of a daycare centre in Perth, causing injuries to a four-year-old boy. Emergency services attended the scene and the child was taken for medical treatment. No further details on the driver or cause were provided.

headline: Inquest opened into police shooting of 16-year-old in Perth car park
summary: A coronial inquest has begun into the fatal police shooting of a 16-year-old boy, described as radicalised, at a Bunnings car park in Perth. The inquiry will examine the circumstances surrounding the incident and the actions of the officer involved.

headline: NSW Premier Minns drops underquoting reforms amid housing slump backlash
summary: New South Wales Premier Chris Minns has shelved proposed underquoting legislation that would have forced real-estate agents to disclose price expectations to buyers. The decision follows a slowdown in the housing market and strong opposition from Sydney agents.

headline: Cape Town baboon relocation to sanctuary sparks protests
summary: Authorities in Cape Town began moving a troop of 44 baboons from Simon’s Town to a wildlife sanctuary, prompting demonstrators to block the transport. Officials say the relocation is needed to reduce human-wildlife conflict, while locals oppose the capture.

headline: Queensland police review use of unofficial AI-powered app
summary: Queensland Police are examining the deployment of an unofficial AI-driven application used by frontline officers after concerns were raised about its governance and data handling. The review follows broader scrutiny of AI tools in public sector operations.

headline: Opinion piece links wartime leaks to technology insiders
summary: A commentary argues that recent leaks of sensitive information may be traced to technology experts, suggesting a new dimension to espionage in modern conflicts.

headline: WA Police investigate complaints about Labor MP’s alleged debts
summary: Western Australian police have received complaints concerning alleged debts of Labor MP Jagadish Krishnan. The force confirmed the matters are under investigation.

headline: Inquest probes deaths of four babies born at home in northern NSW
summary: A coronial inquest is examining the circumstances surrounding the deaths of four infants born at home in northern New South Wales, including a mother’s fear of being forced into a caesarean section if she sought hospital care.

headline: Conjoined twin girls born in remote PNG, possible treatment in Australia
summary: Medical teams in a remote part of Papua New Guinea have delivered conjoined twin girls, marking the country’s second such case in just over a year. Authorities are exploring the possibility of transferring the infants to Australia for specialised care.

headline: European banks adopt AI to cut routine work but profit impact unclear
summary: Banks across Europe are deploying artificial intelligence to automate routine tasks, redeploy staff and recruit technical talent. While the technology promises efficiency gains, its effect on overall profitability remains uncertain.

headline: Rare EF1 tornado touches down in Delaware, causing property damage
summary: An EF1 tornado struck the Salem Woods neighbourhood of Newark, Delaware, damaging roofs, windows and a hotel sign, and overturning a semi-truck on I-95. No injuries or fatalities were reported.

headline: Swans players Heeney and Warner train after police clearance
summary: Sydney Swans stars Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner resumed training with teammates at Centennial Park following their clearance by police in connection with a hotel-room incident earlier this year.

headline: IMF chief warns AI-linked circular financing reaches $1 trillion
summary: Kristalina Georgieva said that circular financing for AI companies has grown to just over $1 trillion, with two-thirds in debt, as investor enthusiasm cools and global economic risks rise.

headline: Kangaroos credit doubters for World Cup triumph
summary: Australian rugby league stars said criticism of their abilities motivated the team, which went on to win the World Cup, highlighting the role of external scepticism in their success.

headline: Inquest begins into Queensland island fire deaths
summary: A coronial inquest has started into the blaze that killed a father and five children on a small Queensland island in 2023, seeking to determine the cause of the tragedy.

headline: Rugby Australia vows to fight players’ union legal challenge
summary: CEO Phil Waugh described the players’ union’s pay and conditions case as an aggressive, costly and avoidable legal battle, confirming Rugby Australia will defend the matter in court.

headline: Government scores poorly on every performance metric
summary: A new poll shows the current Australian government lagging on all measured performance indicators, with cost of living remaining the top concern for voters for the fifth consecutive year.

headline: Australia issues 30-year bonds as yields rise
summary: The Treasury launched a 30-year sovereign bond offering weeks after multi-decade high yields, attracting strong demand from global investors seeking long-term Australian debt.

headline: Metrics takes over distressed property assets
summary: Non-bank lender Metrics placed two property developers into receivership and listed a foreclosed retail strip for sale as defaults in the sector continue to rise.

headline: Severe weather forces 104 Sydney Airport flight cancellations
summary: Adverse weather conditions at Sydney Airport led to major delays and the cancellation of 104 flights, disrupting travel plans for thousands of passengers.

headline: UK, allies urge Israel to speed humanitarian aid to Gaza
summary: The United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Italy called on Israeli authorities to allow rapid delivery of essential supplies, including 150,000 tents, to Gaza, saying restrictions at border crossings were hindering humanitarian assistance.

headline: Test cricket hopefuls miss final selection window
summary: With the New Zealand series squad imminent, prospects Sam Konstas and Jack Clayton failed to impress in the One-Day Cup, losing their last chance to earn a Test debut.

headline: Qantas travel disruptions strand island residents
summary: Passengers from Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands were left stranded on the mainland after Qantas cancelled multiple flights, prompting frustration among island communities.

headline: Opposition says key details omitted from Torrens-Darlington briefing
summary: Opposition figures claim the $15.4 billion Torrens to Darlington infrastructure project briefing left out critical information about a contractor later suspended over alleged bikie links.

headline: Judge’s Facebook posts not enough to overturn abuse ruling
summary: A court dismissed Stephen Fane Noga’s appeal against a verdict that found him liable for sexual abuse of a former student in the 1980s, ruling his social-media activity did not merit a reversal.

headline: Darwin Private Hospital to continue services after takeover delay
summary: The Northern Territory health minister urged patients to keep scheduled procedures at Darwin Private Hospital despite Calvary Health Care postponing its acquisition date.

headline: Greens weigh alternative 40% CGT discount proposal
summary: The Australian Greens are considering a simpler capital gains tax discount model proposed by teal MP Tim Spender, which could challenge the government’s current CGT reform plans.

headline: Lendlease faces investor scepticism over bond redemption plan
summary: Lendlease said its bond redemption was part of proactive capital management, but investors remain unconvinced. The company’s sticky covenant and unexpected move have raised concerns about its financial strategy and market confidence.

headline: Aboriginal teen becomes youngest world surfing champion
summary: An Australian Aboriginal teenager made history by winning the world surfing title, becoming the sport’s youngest champion. The achievement highlights the rising talent and diversity in Australian surfing.

headline: Authors and creators push back against AI copyright lobbying
summary: Australia’s government push to attract AI investment has sparked a campaign by authors, musicians and TV producers. The creative sector argues the policy favours AI firms and threatens copyright protections.

headline: Anti-hype pitch to back record-size IPO gains traction
summary: Dario Amodei’s low-profile approach is being used to support what could become the largest initial public offering. Clients have been told order sizes may be trimmed by about 40 per cent as the deal progresses.

headline: NSW police sexual misconduct allegations revealed in review
summary: A culture review of the NSW Police Force uncovered claims of sexual harassment and assault by officers against fellow uniformed staff. The findings have prompted calls for further investigation and reforms.

headline: Rare 16th-century ‘Book of Miracles’ to be auctioned for £1 million
summary: The ‘Book of Miracles’, a 16th-century manuscript depicting apocalyptic scenes such as five suns over Leipzig and blood rain in Rome, is set to be auctioned. Public institutions will have the first chance to bid.

headline: Sydney Airport flights disrupted after safety directive
summary: Airservices issued a safety directive that forced airlines to slow arrivals and increase spacing due to low cloud, resulting in 92 flight cancellations and 347 delays at Sydney Airport on Monday.

headline: Usman Khawaja discusses racism and mental health in cricket
summary: Australian cricketer Usman Khawaja opened up about experiencing racist stereotyping, his sense of belonging, and early mental-health struggles linked to cricket setbacks, expanding the conversation beyond the Sandpapergate controversy.

headline: UK Labour leader says Brexit has failed ahead of EU summit
summary: Labour Prime Minister Andy Burnham will argue at the upcoming UK-EU summit that Brexit “has not worked” and propose a new deal with the EU, claiming it could raise Britain’s GDP by 0.4 per cent. The comments come amid renewed debate over the post-Brexit relationship.

headline: Victorian town opposes AI data centre at former quarry
summary: Residents of Miners Rest, Victoria, are campaigning against a proposed AI data centre slated for the town’s old quarry, fearing it would disrupt their quiet rural lifestyle.

headline: James Packer’s large Nvidia stake highlighted amid scandal
summary: Billionaire James Packer’s significant investment in Nvidia has come under scrutiny, with reports noting his broader exposure to the tech giant through his Firmus holdings.

headline: Tasmanian author demands apology from premier over Christmas backlash
summary: Best-selling parenting author Biddulph has called on Tasmania’s premier to issue an unreserved apology after a social-media storm over the state’s Christmas celebrations.

headline: Humm faces board battle as director resigns and activist seeks seat
summary: Non-bank lender Humm is in turmoil after a director’s resignation and activist investor Jeremy Raper’s push for a board seat, intensifying a power struggle between founder Andrew Abercrombie and top shareholder.

headline: NSW anti-slavery commissioner refers labour hire syndicate crimes to police
summary: The NSW Anti-slavery Commissioner has referred allegations that labour hire syndicates kidnapped and blackmailed migrant workers to police, highlighting concerns over exploitation in the state’s labour market.

headline: NSW shelves new real estate advertising rules
summary: The NSW government has abandoned planned reforms that would have required property agents to display selling prices or price ranges, cancelling the changes a day before they were to take effect.

headline: PIMCO warns of sustained diesel shortage in Australia
summary: Asset manager PIMCO says the fallout from the US-Iran crisis could lead to a prolonged diesel crunch in Australia, urging an “all-energy” approach to meet rising demand.

headline: Severe thunderstorms bring snow-like hail to southern Queensland
summary: Heavy thunderstorms across southern Queensland produced hail up to 10 cm in size and wind gusts of 91 km/h, prompting warnings for residents in the affected areas.

headline: Jackdaw gas field receives UK government approval
summary: UK ministers have given the green light for gas production at the Jackdaw field, located 150 miles east of Aberdeen, after years of regulatory uncertainty.

headline: Court hears DNA link to Adelaide paediatrician murder suspect
summary: During a hearing, DNA matching murder-accused Kerem Aydin was reportedly found at the scene where Adelaide paediatrician Michael Yung was killed in 2023.

headline: Statue unveiled to honour Merle Thornton’s 1965 protest
summary: A new statue in Brisbane commemorates Merle Thornton, who chained herself to a bar in 1965 to protest the ban on women in Queensland public bars.

headline: Proposed on-shore gas bill faces constitutional challenge
summary: The coalition and Greens oppose a new bill that would require LNG exporters to supply a greater share of gas to Australian consumers, citing constitutional concerns.

headline: NRL highlights to be free for podcasters from 2028
summary: From 2028, podcasters covering the NRL will be allowed to use footage and highlight reels from Nine and Foxtel at no cost, subject to certain conditions.

headline: Beaconsfield miner Todd Russell remembered after death
summary: Former Beaconsfield miner Todd Russell was remembered for his humour and reflections on his funeral plans, recalling a previous burial he did not enjoy.

headline: Forrestania secures 72.5% stake in Zenith Minerals
summary: Forrestania Resources has completed a takeover offer, acquiring a 72.56 per cent controlling interest in Zenith Minerals. The deal advances Forrestania’s strategy to consolidate gold assets in Western Australia and brings Zenith under its operational umbrella.

headline: Australians at forefront of global AI safety efforts
summary: Dozens of Australians have relocated to San Francisco to work for leading AI labs or the surrounding AI safety ecosystem. They are actively raising concerns about the risk of artificial intelligence systems becoming uncontrolled.

headline: Gateway Mining reports high-grade gold find at Yandal project
summary: Gateway Mining announced a shallow, high-grade gold discovery at its Yandal project near Wiluna, Western Australia. Recent reverse-circulation drilling returned 11 metres at 4.5 g/t gold from 89 metres depth, confirming a new mineralised system.

headline: Westfield seeks new anchors as David Jones administrators meet creditors
summary: The owner of Westfield shopping centres has intensified pressure on administrators of David Jones, with meetings scheduled with creditors. Westfield is exploring replacement tenants for the department store’s locations across its Australian malls.

headline: UK ministers warned weakening EV targets would hurt car industry
summary: Experts told UK ministers that diluting the zero-emission vehicle mandate would slow market growth, raise costs for consumers and undermine the country's net-zero objectives, potentially harming the domestic automotive sector.

headline: Home Office criticised for attempting to cancel Andreas Malm online talk
summary: The Home Office faced accusations of trying to block an online event featuring climate academic Andreas Malm. Hackney mayor Shadwell decried the move as an assault on free speech after the talk proceeded despite warnings.

headline: England plans reforms to expand appeals for special-needs support
summary: Proposed changes to England’s special-needs education system could give families new routes to appeal for additional school support, including ombudsman reviews, amid criticism that current reforms dilute legal protections.

headline: Police shooting of 16-year-old extremist and trial of ex-officer draws scrutiny
summary: A coronial inquest heard that 16-year-old James Hollands, who sent a jihad-related text, was shot by police after a knife attack. Former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, charged with double murder, faced cross-examination and later re-examination by his own barrister during the trial.

headline: Allens bolsters M&A practice hiring Hamilton Locke senior partner
summary: Allens has expanded its mergers and acquisitions team, bringing in senior partner Hamilton Locke from Hamilton Locke. The move follows the firm’s ongoing effort to grow its M&A and capital markets capabilities.

headline: Travis Auld steps down as Australian Grand Prix Corp CEO
summary: Travis Auld has resigned as chief executive of the Australian Grand Prix Corporation. He will not disclose his next employer or the location of his new role, and his departure comes ahead of the upcoming Formula 1 season.

headline: Police release CCTV footage of fatal drive-by shooting
summary: Detectives from the Logan Criminal Investigation Branch have released CCTV footage showing a blue Mazda 2 near Bryants Road at the time of a fatal drive-by shooting. The video is being circulated to aid the investigation and encourage anyone with information to come forward.

headline: Report flags dysfunction at Serpentine Jarrahdale council
summary: An independent monitor’s report on the Shire of Serpentine Jarrahdale highlights concerns over councillor behaviour and psychosocial safety. The findings suggest systemic issues within the council and call for reforms to improve governance and staff wellbeing.

headline: Health Minister Butler urges states to allow puberty blockers
summary: Health Minister Mark Butler has challenged states and territories that have banned puberty blockers for children to follow new national guidelines. He says the guidelines are based on medical consensus and that denying access could harm young people’s health.

headline: EU envoy urges Australian government to back trade pact
summary: The new EU ambassador said the bloc would consider climate-assurance requests if the Australian government proposes a win-win trade deal. He described the potential agreement as a “bloody good deal” and urged the Coalition to support the negotiations.

headline: AFR launches indices to broaden ASX investment view
summary: The Australian Financial Review has introduced a suite of indices designed to give a wider economic perspective on ASX opportunities. The launch is positioned as the next step in strengthening Australia’s capital-markets infrastructure and supporting investors.

headline: Lucy Wicks responds to stalking allegations by MP Taylor Martin
summary: NSW MP Taylor Martin accused former staffer Lucy Wicks of stalking him in a parliamentary speech. Wicks has now publicly replied, denying the claims and defending her conduct amid the political dispute.

headline: Rex posts losses as US owner fails to restore fleet
summary: Regional airline Rex reported a loss after its US owner, tasked with returning planes to service, has not added a single aircraft in almost a year. The ongoing issues raise concerns about the airline’s expansion plans.

headline: Mother describes grief after son killed by 16-year-old
summary: A mother recounted the “unbearable” grief she feels after her son, Jack Westren, who had a brain injury, was ambushed and murdered by a group of teenagers at Shellharbour Junction train station.

headline: Sam Walker to discuss PNG Chiefs move with club officials
summary: Off-contract Roosters centre Sam Walker will meet PNG Chiefs officials on Tuesday to explore a potential transfer to the expansion franchise, where he could partner with Jarome Luai in the halves.

headline: Witness testimony ends in Lamarre-Condon court case
summary: The Crown prosecutor concluded the witness testimony of Beau Lamarre-Condon, reading statements from Jesse Baird’s brother and Luke Davies’s mother relating to evidence given by the accused, marking the end of that phase of the trial.

headline: Critical Resources gains access to high-grade antimony prospect
summary: Critical Resources has secured ground access to its Mayview antimony-gold prospect in NSW, where rock chip samples returned 52.3 % antimony, located just 2.7 km from the existing Hillgrove mine.

headline: Ken Wyatt appointed WA’s first Indigenous governor
summary: Former federal minister Ken Wyatt, the first Indigenous Australian elected to the House of Representatives, has been named Western Australia’s inaugural Indigenous governor, marking a historic first for the state.

headline: Albanese urged to boycott photo with Putin at APEC
summary: Critics have called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to avoid a photo-op with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit, warning it could normalise Russia’s standing and undermine Australia’s support for Ukraine.

headline: Judge rejects bid to keep Kmart child sex offender in prison
summary: A Queensland judge dismissed an application to keep a man convicted of child sexual offences at Kmart, allowing his release. The offender had lured a child from a mother in the toy aisle of a Westfield store in 2018. The decision follows legal arguments about his continued detention.

headline: Mother of five killed in Russell Island fire gives evidence at inquest
summary: A mother whose partner and five sons perished in a house fire on Russell Island has begun testifying at the inquest into the tragedy. She described the blaze as being everywhere and recounted the devastating loss of her family as investigators examine the cause of the fire.

headline: Australia joins US-led Pax Silica AI supply-chain pact
summary: Australia became a founding member of Pax Silica, a US-initiated alliance aimed at safeguarding AI supply chains from Chinese influence. The pact brings together seven countries to coordinate on rare-earth and semiconductor security, reflecting growing concerns over Beijing’s dominance in advanced technology components.

headline: Widow of Haiti’s assassinated leader registers for presidential race
summary: The wife of former Haitian president Jovenel Moïse, assassinated in 2021, has filed paperwork to run in the upcoming presidential election. Haiti has not held a national vote since the killing, and her candidacy marks a rare entry of a former first lady into the political arena.

headline: Independent MP Helen Haines discharged after hospitalisation
summary: Helen Haines, the independent MP who was attacked outside her office, has been released from hospital and entered the rehabilitation stage. She thanked supporters and donors for their messages and charity contributions. The attack resulted in double amputation of her legs, and she is now focusing on recovery.

headline: Barrenjoey tops broker survey as equities desks light up
summary: Barrenjoey Capital Partners was ranked first in the latest Peter Lee broker survey, outperforming peers across equity research and sales. The results highlight the firm’s strong performance on the Australian equities desk and its growing influence among institutional investors.

headline: Tax regulator pursues former KPMG manager over unauthorised GST refunds
summary: The Australian Taxation Office has launched action against Anthony George Confos, a former KPMG manager, for allegedly lodging unauthorised GST refunds and diverting nearly $1 million to personal accounts. The case underscores ongoing scrutiny of tax-avoidance schemes.

headline: Victorian premier says documents withheld from royal commission
summary: Premier Ben Carroll accused officials of withholding documents from the commission investigating the Big Build, while Health Minister Ingrid Stitt denied briefing claims. The dispute comes as the state government pushes free prenatal testing amid fears of an upcoming election loss.

headline: Former EY partner found to have promoted illegal tax schemes
summary: The Australian Taxation Office secured a court victory against former EY partner Peter White, who was found to have advised wealthy clients on unlawful tax structures. The ruling represents a significant enforcement action against professional misconduct in tax advisory services.

headline: UK ministers criticised for not knowing cost of NHS maternity repairs
summary: NHS chiefs warned that 43 percent of maternity and neonatal units in England fail to meet safety standards, accusing ministers of “gambling with safety” after admitting they lack knowledge of the repair costs for deteriorating facilities. The criticism highlights systemic infrastructure issues in the health system.

headline: Spain prepares for snap election that could bring far-right to power
summary: Spain will hold a snap general election on 29 November, its sixth in 11 years, with the possibility of a far-right party entering government for the first time since the Franco era. The vote could end eight years of socialist rule and reshape the political landscape.

headline: EU to propose €45 billion loan for Ukraine funded by EU budget
summary: The European Commission will present a proposal to lend Ukraine €45 billion, to be financed from the EU’s own budget. The loan aims to bridge Kyiv’s funding gap for the coming year and is part of the bloc’s broader support for the war-torn nation.

headline: Top 2026 IPOs tumble over 20% as AI hype fades
summary: The ten largest initial public offerings of the year have lost more than a fifth of their value on average, reflecting a slowdown in investor enthusiasm for artificial-intelligence driven companies after years of strong gains.

headline: Migration to rich nations slows sharply, adding fiscal strain
summary: A steep decline in the number of migrants arriving in wealthy countries is intensifying fiscal challenges linked to rapidly ageing populations, according to recent analysis.

summary: Australian universities that rank highly for teaching are examining how artificial intelligence will shape learning and testing. While AI can generate answers instantly, institutions stress the need to continue building curated knowledge and robust assessment methods.

summary: Research highlights that while household chores are often shared, financial decisions frequently fall to a single person, creating a hidden mental load that can lead to burnout.

summary: The Financial Review introduces its own suite of indices to give readers clearer signals on the overall economy and the performance of its most global Australian companies, aiming to aid investment decisions.

summary: As the Reserve Bank’s rate hikes bite, the number of borrowers falling behind on mortgage repayments is climbing and is expected to rise further, signalling growing pressure on households.

summary: A fast-food brand that impressed Prime Minister Anthony Albanese during a visit to its Manila outlet is preparing to launch in Australia, adding another player to the crowded chicken-focused quick-service sector.

summary: One Nation’s electoral prospects in Victoria are under scrutiny ahead of the state election, with party founder Pauline Hanson notably missing from the campaign trail.

summary: Leading Australian research universities are looking to Europe for fresh funding sources as domestic research budgets tighten, exploring structural reforms, international collaborations and spin-out start-ups to sustain their programmes.

summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a comprehensive overhaul of support for young people, promising early-stage interventions and a benefits backstop to address the youth jobs crisis in Britain.

summary: Clothing factories in Bangladesh have halted production after workers launched a strike demanding a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) per month.

summary: The Port of New Orleans has filed a $1 million lawsuit following a collision between a tanker and a cruise ship on the Mississippi River. The suit seeks damages and requests that the tanker be seized and sold to cover the costs of the incident.
