summary: Two days after a nationwide grounding of aircraft, thousands of US flights are still cancelled or delayed, with the transport secretary warning that normal operations may not resume until Monday.

summary: The Australian Wallabies enter their test against Scotland needing a win to avoid a fourth consecutive defeat. The match features two familiar faces for Scotland and is being followed live.

summary: A final report by former Labour minister Alan Milburn calls for reforms to address the growing number of young people not in education, employment or training. summary: Commentary suggests Woolworths is set to pull ahead in the ongoing supermarket rivalry, with market sentiment shifting in its favour as the two giants battle for share.

summary: Supporters of Test captain Pat Cummins are divided, with some fans questioning his standing against fellow player Usman Khawaja as discussions swirl on social media.

summary: Artificial-intelligence tools are being used to analyse Kurt Gödel’s 1,009 pages of handwritten notes, which may contain hundreds of previously unknown theorems.

headline: DC condo shooter confessed over living-condition dispute
summary: The gunman responsible for killing one person and injuring several others near a Washington, D.C. condominium told a manager he acted out of anger over his living conditions.

headline: Public stockpiles emergency supplies amid uncertainty
summary: Consumers are buying items such as cider and candy canes as part of a growing trend of emergency stockpiling.

headline: Jaguar Land Rover posts £451 million loss after job cuts
summary: JLR reported a £451 million quarterly loss, citing £530 million in costs linked to the recent reduction of 4,000 jobs, while revenue rose to £5.9 billion.

headline: Metropolitan Police investigate David Walliams
summary: London police have opened a criminal investigation into comedian David Walliams following multiple allegations of sexual misconduct involving young women and teenagers.

headline: Prince William edits Country Life issue
summary: The Prince of Wales contributed a personal piece to Country Life, sharing his love of the countryside and offering a glimpse into his rural lifestyle.

headline: Veteran rebuilds credit after living in car
summary: A former service member turned his financial situation around, achieving a 756 credit score after a period of homelessness in his car.

headline: Fourteen dividend stocks highlighted for growth
summary: Analyst John Buckingham recommends 14 dividend-paying companies that appear undervalued and offer strong long-term growth potential.

headline: UK-EU plant-trade deal to cut £60 million costs
summary: The new post-Brexit agreement will remove border checks on plant imports, eliminating about £60 million in annual expenses for the horticulture sector, though firms won’t recover past costs.

headline: Menopause linked to pay cuts and career setbacks
summary: Women, as well as some trans and non-binary people, report financial and professional setbacks during menopause, describing the experience as “white-knuckling” and feeling sidelined at work.

headline: Thai-style salads boost popularity of shopping centre eatery
summary: A shopping centre restaurant draws neighbours with bold northern Thai dishes and a karaoke room, offering a fresh take on robust salads.

headline: Democratic Senate leader Schumer faces internal leadership challenge
summary: Senator Van Hollen says new leadership is needed for Democrats after recent midterm successes, signalling a potential challenge to Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer.

headline: Wholesale prices rise 0.3% in October, annual rate hits four-year high
summary: The producer price index increased by 0.3% in October, putting the annual wholesale price growth at 6.5%, the strongest pace in almost four years, ahead of expectations for a 0.4% monthly rise.

headline: Germany grants spies expanded powers to counter hybrid threats
summary: New legislation gives German foreign and domestic intelligence agencies broader authority to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage as part of a response to hybrid threats from abroad.

headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet with major card networks
summary: OpenAI’s new ChatGPT Wallet lets its AI agents make purchases for users, partnering with American Express, Mastercard and Visa while preserving existing credit-card rewards.

headline: UK government considers weakening planning challenge rights
summary: Lawyers warn that the UK may strip legal protections under the Aarhus convention, potentially raising costs for community groups contesting planning decisions that affect the environment.

headline: At least 24 dead after bus-truck collision in northeast India
summary: A bus collided with a truck in northeast India, killing at least 24 people, including several college students, according to local officials.

headline: Divers explore sunken ship off Florida as new artificial reef
summary: Divers are investigating a ship deliberately sunk off Florida’s coast, intended to become the world’s largest artificial ocean reef.

headline: NHL TV rights deal to test league amid rising media costs
summary: The upcoming NHL television contract will gauge the league’s strength as media companies adjust to higher rights fees, especially after NFL deals increase market values.

headline: Advisors weigh Nvidia exposure after CEO exit and stock dip
summary: Following Jensen Huang’s departure and a sharp fall in Nvidia’s share price, financial advisers recommend investors consider their risk tolerance, time horizon and overall exposure before reacting to the volatility surrounding the AI-chip maker.

headline: Ireland opens secret room of previously banned books to public
summary: A Dublin justice department building has finally allowed public access to its long-closed “room of evil literature”, which housed around 12,000 titles once deemed indecent or obscene, spanning publications from 1926 to 1996.

headline: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee warns inflation still a concern
summary: Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee told CNBC that recent inflation data keep the central bank’s work unfinished, signalling that further policy action may be needed to bring price growth under control.

headline: Shoplifters in Scotland resort to weapons amid rising thefts
summary: Shop workers in Scotland report a surge in violent shoplifting, with thieves using harpoon guns and machetes as they target stores, prompting concerns over safety and loss prevention.

headline: Liberal candidate Jess Wilson tours country pubs to court voters
summary: Liberal hopeful Jess Wilson took the “Jess Express” to a country pub on the Victorian-New South Wales border, seeking to win over local voters ahead of a tightly contested seat, while noting competition from One Nation.

headline: Sydney worker takes pizza jobs as cost of living squeezes Australians
summary: Vanessa Freitas, a Brazilian-born Sydney resident, now delivers pizza after work to help pay rent, reflecting growing financial stress among Australians facing interest-rate hikes, price rises and job cuts.

headline: NSW premier backs coal port expansion despite climate criticism
summary: New South Wales Premier Chris Minns approved the state’s largest coal-mine expansion at the Hunter Valley, drawing criticism for ignoring climate concerns and potential health impacts while positioning the project as an economic driver.

headline: Tough Guy Book Club encourages men to read, reaches 10,000 members
summary: Founded by Shay Leighton, the Tough Guy Book Club promotes reading among men, operating out of Australian pubs and now boasting 10,000 participants worldwide, aiming to break stereotypes around masculinity and literacy.

headline: Labor’s tax reforms face scrutiny amid falling house prices
summary: The Albanese government’s recent tax changes are under pressure as property values decline. Critics argue the measures need stronger justification, especially as the prime minister’s overseas trips to the Caribbean and Turkey draw public ire over domestic cost-of-living concerns.

headline: Iran says it hit US early-warning radar in Bahrain
summary: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for a US airstrike on a communications tower, marking the first direct attack on US military installations in months.

headline: CFTC chair says crypto firms embracing new agency rules
summary: CFTC Chair Rostin Behnam told CNBC that the crypto industry is increasingly complying with the regulator’s proposed rules, even as broader legislative efforts to govern digital assets lose momentum.

headline: Former Ukrainian PM aide wounded in Moscow car bomb attack
summary: Sergei Zavorotny, once an adviser to former Ukrainian prime minister Mykola Azarov, was injured in a recent car bombing in Moscow. The incident adds to a series of attacks targeting figures linked to the Ukraine-Russia conflict.

headline: Trump says he wants to resolve Cuba issue before leaving office
summary: Former US president Donald Trump stated he intends to "get Cuba done" before his term ends, hinting at possible military action while the United States continues its comprehensive economic embargo on the island.

headline: NHL team valuations rise 23% to average $2.71 billion
summary: CNBC reports the average value of the 32 National Hockey League franchises has climbed to $2.71 billion, a 23 percent increase from a year ago, reflecting growing revenue and media deals.

headline: New York landfill expansion plan meets resident opposition
summary: A company proposes to raise the height of the Seneca Meadows landfill in upstate New York, extending its lifespan for decades despite concerns from nearby residents about smell and environmental impact.

headline: Moscow urges Europe to appoint envoy for dialogue
summary: Russia tells European nations to select a diplomatic representative if they wish Moscow to engage in talks, after EU foreign minister Kaja Kallas said President Vladimir Putin refuses to speak with her.

headline: UN watchdog raises concerns over uninspected Iranian nuclear site
summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency says it has never been able to inspect Iran's uranium enrichment plant at Isfahan, expressing increasing worry about the lack of access to the facility.

headline: Russian crude output rebounds as global oil supply tops demand
summary: Russia's crude production rose to 8.73 million barrels per day in October, according to the IEA, helping push worldwide oil supply into surplus amid recovering Gulf exports.

headline: US seizes $1.2 billion of crypto linked to North Korean theft
summary: The Department of Justice announced the seizure of $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance, targeting a scheme used by the North Korean regime to fund its activities.

headline: Microsoft Outlook outage disrupts US organisations
summary: A widespread Outlook outage that began on Thursday afternoon left many US companies, schools and local governments unable to access email, calendar and cloud services, with some services still down despite partial restoration on Friday.

headline: Albanese and Bowen caught on hot mic joking about phones
summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Energy Minister Jim Bowen were unaware a microphone was live when they made jokes about where they keep their mobile phones.

headline: Rosalía wins historic third best album award at Latin Grammys
summary: Spanish singer Rosalía received the award for best album for her fourth release, Lux, marking a historic third win in the category at the Latin Grammy Awards.

headline: Four students die after post-exam party at Nigerian university
summary: A Nigerian university is in mourning after four students died following a post-exam celebration; the institution has banned all parties while investigations continue.

headline: Australian athletes win sprint events at national meets
summary: Sam Short edged out Harrison Turner in the men's 400m sprint, while William Petric claimed victory in the men's 200m mystery medley at recent Australian track meets. Both athletes secured their titles in tightly contested races, adding to the season's sprint highlights.

headline: Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon convicted of child rape
summary: A jury found former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon guilty of one count of sexual intercourse with a child aged 10-14 and indecent assault after a four-hour deliberation. The conviction follows a previous trial that ended with a hung jury, and Amon faces a significant prison term.
